[Constitution of Montenegro](./Constitution_of_Montenegro \"Constitution of Montenegro\")\\n\\nThe current [Constitution of Montenegro](./Constitution_of_Montenegro \"Constitution of Montenegro\") was ratified and adopted by the [Constitutional Parliament](./Parliament_of_Montenegro \"Parliament of Montenegro\") of Montenegro on 19 October 2007 in a session by achieving the required two-thirds [supermajority](./Supermajority \"Supermajority\") of votes.[[141]](./Montenegro#cite_note-147)[[142]](./Montenegro#cite_note-148) It was officially proclaimed on 22 October 2007.[[143]](./Montenegro#cite_note-149)\\n\\nThe Constitution defines Montenegro as a civic, [democratic](./Democracy \"Democracy\") and [environmentally friendly](./Environmentally_friendly \"Environmentally friendly\") country with [social justice](./Social_justice \"Social justice\"), established by the [sovereign rights](./Sovereign_rights \"Sovereign rights\") of its government.[[144]](./Montenegro#cite_note-Pobjeda-150)[[145]](./Montenegro#cite_note-CafedelMontenegro-151)\\n\\nThe judiciary in Montenegro is composed of several courts, with the Supreme Court being the highest judicial authority. It oversees the uniform application of laws. Administrative Courts handle disputes related to public administration. The judiciary also includes Basic Courts (for minor civil and criminal cases), High Courts (for more serious cases and appeals), and the Appellate Court for reviewing lower court decisions.\\n\\nThe Constitutional Court is a separate body, tasked with safeguarding the constitution by reviewing laws and acts of public authorities to ensure their compliance with the Constitution.\\n\\nJudges in Montenegro are appointed by the Judicial Council and serve until the age of 67. The [President of Montenegro](./President_of_Montenegro \"President of Montenegro\") appoints judges upon the recommendation of the Judicial Council. Additionally, the Protector of Human Rights and Freedoms of Montenegro (Ombudsman) is appointed by the Parliament for a six-year term, ensuring the protection of human rights and social justice.\\n\\nDiscrimination on the basis of both [sexual orientation](./Sexual_orientation \"Sexual orientation\") and [gender identity](./Gender_identity \"Gender identity\") is banned in employment, the provision of goods and services, education and health services. Montenegro also possesses [hate crime](./Hate_crime \"Hate crime\") and [hate speech](./Hate_speech \"Hate speech\") laws which include sexual orientation and gender identity as grounds of non-discrimination.\\nSince 15 July 2021, same-sex couples may register their relationship as a [Life Partnership](./Recognition_of_same-sex_unions_in_Montenegro \"Recognition of same-sex unions in Montenegro\").\\n\\n### Law enforcement, security and emergency services\\n\\nMain article: [Police Directorate of Montenegro](./Police_Directorate_of_Montenegro \"Police Directorate of Montenegro\")\\n\\nLaw enforcement in Montenegro is carried out by several agencies under the [Ministry of Interior](./Ministry_of_Interior_(Montenegro) \"Ministry of Interior (Montenegro)\").\\nCivil law enforcement in Montenegro is primarily the responsibility of the Police Directorate, the national police force. [Municipal police](./Municipal_police \"Municipal police\"), known as Communal Police, enforce local laws in their respective municipalities.[[146]](./Montenegro#cite_note-152)\\n\\nLaw enforcement in Montenegro is carried out by several agencies under the [Ministry of Interior](./Ministry_of_Interior_(Montenegro) \"Ministry of Interior (Montenegro)\").\\nThe primary law enforcement body is the Montenegrin Police Directorate, responsible for crime investigation, maintaining public order, and general law enforcement. The Municipal Police assist with local law enforcement tasks, primarily focusing on traffic regulation and minor public order issues.[[147]](./Montenegro#cite_note-153)\\nPrivate security firms operate in Montenegro but have no legal authority to arrest or detain suspects.\\n\\nThe [National Security Agency (ANB)](./National_Security_Agency_(Montenegro) \"National Security Agency (Montenegro)\") is responsible for counterintelligence and internal security, while Interpol Montenegro collaborates with international agencies to counter transnational crime. Special units within the police, such as the Special Anti-Terrorist Unit (SAJ), handle organized crime, terrorism, and high-risk operations.\\n\\nAn agreement signed with the [EU](./EU \"EU\") effective July 2023 permits EU [Frontex](./Frontex \"Frontex\") border management personnel to operate in Montenegro in support of local border police operating on other, non EU, borders in Montenegro.[[148]](./Montenegro#cite_note-154)\\n\\nEmergency services in Montenegro include medical services, firefighters, and search and rescue units, which are coordinated by the Directorate for Emergency Situations. Emergency medical services are operated by local health institutions but are overseen by the [Ministry of Health](./Ministry_of_Health_(Montenegro) \"Ministry of Health (Montenegro)\").\\n\\n### Military\\n\\nMain article: [Armed Forces of Montenegro](./Armed_Forces_of_Montenegro \"Armed Forces of Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/45/Final_formation_%287168937179%29.jpg/250px-Final_formation_%287168937179%29.jpg)](./File:Final_formation_(7168937179).jpg)\\n\\n[Montenegrin army soldiers](./Armed_Forces_of_Montenegro \"Armed Forces of Montenegro\") with [NATO](./NATO \"NATO\") allies in [Slunj](./Slunj \"Slunj\"), [Croatia](./Croatia \"Croatia\")\\n\\nThe military of Montenegro consist of three professional service branches: the [Montenegrin Ground Army](./Montenegrin_Ground_Army \"Montenegrin Ground Army\"), the [Montenegrin Navy](./Montenegrin_Navy \"Montenegrin Navy\") and the [Montenegrin Air Force](./Montenegrin_Air_Force \"Montenegrin Air Force\"). The armed forces of Montenegro are managed by the [Ministry of Defence](./Ministry_of_Defence_(Montenegro) \"Ministry of Defence (Montenegro)\"), and controlled by the Chief of the General Staff. The [President of Montenegro](./President_of_Montenegro \"President of Montenegro\") is the [Commander-in-Chief](./Commander-in-Chief \"Commander-in-Chief\") of the armed forces, to whom members of the forces swear an oath of allegiance. The Armed Forces are charged with protecting Montenegro, promoting the global security interests and supporting international peacekeeping efforts.\\n\\nMontenegro is a NATO member and a member of [Adriatic Charter](./Adriatic_Charter \"Adriatic Charter\").[[149]](./Montenegro#cite_note-155)[[150]](./Montenegro#cite_note-156) The government planned to have the army participate in [peacekeeping](./Peacekeeping \"Peacekeeping\") missions through the UN and NATO such as the [International Security Assistance Force](./International_Security_Assistance_Force \"International Security Assistance Force\").[[151]](./Montenegro#cite_note-157)\\n\\nMontenegro is the 35th most peaceful country in the world, according to the 2024 [Global Peace Index](./Global_Peace_Index \"Global Peace Index\").[[152]](./Montenegro#cite_note-158)\\n\\nEconomy\\n-------\\n\\nMain article: [Economy of Montenegro](./Economy_of_Montenegro \"Economy of Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/14/Krnovo_Wind_farm_07.jpg/250px-Krnovo_Wind_farm_07.jpg)](./File:Krnovo_Wind_farm_07.jpg)\\n\\nKrnovo Wind farm\\n\\nThe economy of Montenegro is mostly [service-based](./Tertiary_sector_of_the_economy \"Tertiary sector of the economy\") and is in [late transition](./Transition_economy \"Transition economy\") to a [market economy](./Market_economy \"Market economy\"). According to the [International Monetary Fund](./International_Monetary_Fund \"International Monetary Fund\"), the [nominal GDP](./Nominal_GDP \"Nominal GDP\") of Montenegro was $5.424\\xa0billion in 2019.[[153]](./Montenegro#cite_note-IMFWEO.ME-159) The [GDP PPP](./GDP_PPP \"GDP PPP\") for 2019 was $12.516\\xa0billion, or $20,083 per capita.[[153]](./Montenegro#cite_note-IMFWEO.ME-159) According to [Eurostat](./Eurostat \"Eurostat\") data, the Montenegrin GDP per capita stood at 48% of the EU average in 2018.[[154]](./Montenegro#cite_note-160)\\n\\nMontenegro joined the [Central European Free Trade Agreement](./Central_European_Free_Trade_Agreement \"Central European Free Trade Agreement\") in 2007 and has a free trade agreement with the [European Free Trade Association](./European_Free_Trade_Association \"European Free Trade Association\") since 2012. The [Central Bank of Montenegro](./Central_Bank_of_Montenegro \"Central Bank of Montenegro\") is not part of the euro system but the country is \"[euroised](./Euroisation \"Euroisation\")\", using [the euro unilaterally](./Montenegro_and_the_euro \"Montenegro and the euro\") as its currency. Montenegro was ranked 64th in the [Global Innovation Index](./Global_Innovation_Index \"Global Innovation Index\") in 2025,[[155]](./Montenegro#cite_note-161)[[156]](./Montenegro#cite_note-162) up from 75th in 2023.[[157]](./Montenegro#cite_note-163)\\n\\n### Infrastructure\\n\\nMain article: [Transport in Montenegro](./Transport_in_Montenegro \"Transport in Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a8/Montenegro_motorways.JPG/250px-Montenegro_motorways.JPG)](./File:Montenegro_motorways.JPG)\\n\\nRoads of Montenegro in service and planned\\n\\nThe Montenegrin road infrastructure is not at Western European standards. No roads meet full motorway standards. Construction of new motorways is considered a national priority, as they are important for uniform economic development and the development of Montenegro as an attractive tourist destination.\\n\\nThe [European routes](./European_route \"European route\") that pass through Montenegro are [E65](./European_route_E65 \"European route E65\") and [E80](./European_route_E80 \"European route E80\").\\n\\nThe backbone of the Montenegrin rail network is the [Belgrade–Bar railway](./Belgrade–Bar_railway \"Belgrade–Bar railway\"), which provides international connection towards [Serbia](./Serbia \"Serbia\"). A domestic branch line, the [Nikšić-Podgorica railway](./Nikšić-Podgorica_railway \"Nikšić-Podgorica railway\"), operated as a freight-only line for decades, that opened for passenger traffic after reconstruction and electrification in 2012. The other branch line from Podgorica towards the Albanian border, the [Podgorica–Shkodër railway](./Podgorica–Shkodër_railway \"Podgorica–Shkodër railway\"), is not in use.\\n\\nMontenegro has two international airports, [Podgorica Airport](./Podgorica_Airport \"Podgorica Airport\") and [Tivat Airport](./Tivat_Airport \"Tivat Airport\").\\n\\nThe [Port of Bar](./Port_of_Bar \"Port of Bar\") is Montenegro\\'s main seaport. Initially built in 1906, the port was almost completely destroyed during World War II. Reconstruction began in 1950. It is equipped to handle over five million tons of cargo annually, but has been operating at a loss and well below capacity. The reconstruction of the [Belgrade-Bar railway](./Belgrade-Bar_railway \"Belgrade-Bar railway\") and the proposed [Belgrade-Bar motorway](./Belgrade-Bar_motorway \"Belgrade-Bar motorway\") are expected to return operating levels to capacity.\\n\\nIn 2023 there is a plan to install an [LNG](./LNG \"LNG\") terminal at Bar to receive gas imports.[[158]](./Montenegro#cite_note-164)\\n\\n### Tourism\\n\\nMain article: [Tourism in Montenegro](./Tourism_in_Montenegro \"Tourism in Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/56/The_Black_Lake_in_Montenegro.jpg/250px-The_Black_Lake_in_Montenegro.jpg)](./File:The_Black_Lake_in_Montenegro.jpg)\\n\\nThe [Black Lake](./Black_Lake_(Montenegro) \"Black Lake (Montenegro)\") in [Durmitor National Park](./Durmitor_National_Park \"Durmitor National Park\"), a [World Heritage Site](./World_Heritage_Site \"World Heritage Site\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Sveti_Stefan_Montenegro_may_2021_%2810%29.jpg/250px-Sveti_Stefan_Montenegro_may_2021_%2810%29.jpg)](./File:Sveti_Stefan_Montenegro_may_2021_(10).jpg)\\n\\n[Sveti Stefan](./Sveti_Stefan \"Sveti Stefan\")\\n\\nA total of 2.1\\xa0million visitors visited Montenegro in 2022 spending 12.4m nights there.[[159]](./Montenegro#cite_note-165) The majority of foreign visitors to Montenegro come from the neighbouring countries of Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Kosovo, as well as Russia.[[160]](./Montenegro#cite_note-166)\\n\\nThe Montenegrin [Adriatic](./Adriatic \"Adriatic\") coast is 295\\xa0km (183\\xa0mi) long, with 72\\xa0km (45\\xa0mi) of beaches and many well-preserved ancient towns. Some of the most popular beaches include [Jaz Beach](./Jaz_Beach \"Jaz Beach\"), [Mogren Beach](./Budva \"Budva\"), [Bečići Beach](./Bečići \"Bečići\"), [Sveti Stefan Beach](./Sveti_Stefan \"Sveti Stefan\") and [Velika Plaža](./Velika_Plaža \"Velika Plaža\").[[161]](./Montenegro#cite_note-My_Guide_Montenegro-167) Meanwhile, some of the most popular ancient towns include [Herceg Novi](./Herceg_Novi \"Herceg Novi\"), [Perast](./Perast \"Perast\"), [Kotor](./Kotor \"Kotor\"), [Budva](./Budva \"Budva\") and [Ulcinj](./Ulcinj \"Ulcinj\").[[162]](./Montenegro#cite_note-My_Guide_Montenegro_2020-168)\\n\\n*[National Geographic Traveler](./National_Geographic_Traveler \"National Geographic Traveler\")* (edited once a decade) ranks Montenegro among the \"50 Places of a Lifetime\". Montenegrin seaside town [Sveti Stefan](./Sveti_Stefan \"Sveti Stefan\") was once used as the cover for the magazine.[[163]](./Montenegro#cite_note-169) The coast region of Montenegro was considered one of the great \"discoveries\" among world tourists. In January 2010, *[The New York Times](./The_New_York_Times \"The New York Times\")* ranked the Ulcinj South Coast region of Montenegro, including [Velika Plaža](./Velika_Plaža \"Velika Plaža\"), [Ada Bojana](./Ada_Bojana \"Ada Bojana\"), and the [Hotel Mediteran](./Hotel_Mediteran \"Hotel Mediteran\") of Ulcinj, among the \"Top 31 Places to Go in 2010\" as part of a worldwide ranking.[[164]](./Montenegro#cite_note-170)\\n\\nDemographics\\n------------\\n\\nMain articles: [Demographics of Montenegro](./Demographics_of_Montenegro \"Demographics of Montenegro\") and [Demographic history of Montenegro](./Demographic_history_of_Montenegro \"Demographic history of Montenegro\")\\n\\n### Ethnic structure\\n\\nThe 2023 census reported 623,633 citizens.[[165]](./Montenegro#cite_note-t819-171) Montenegro is a [multiethnic state](./Multiethnic_state \"Multiethnic state\") with no ethnic majority.[[166]](./Montenegro#cite_note-172)[[167]](./Montenegro#cite_note-173) [Montenegrins](./Montenegrins \"Montenegrins\") make up 41.1% of the population, [Serbs](./Serbs_of_Montenegro \"Serbs of Montenegro\") 32.9%, [Bosniaks](./Bosniaks_of_Montenegro \"Bosniaks of Montenegro\") 9.45%, [Albanians](./Albanians_in_Montenegro \"Albanians in Montenegro\") 4.99%, and [Russians](./Russians \"Russians\") 2.01%.[[168]](./Montenegro#cite_note-g302-174) There is a significant number of other ethnic groups, including [Romani people](./Romani_people_in_Montenegro \"Romani people in Montenegro\"), [Croats](./Croats_in_Montenegro \"Croats in Montenegro\"), [Ukrainians](./Ukrainians \"Ukrainians\"), [Belarusians](./Belarusians \"Belarusians\"), and [Turks](./Turkish_people \"Turkish people\").\\n\\n### Languages\\n\\nMain article: [Languages of Montenegro](./Languages_of_Montenegro \"Languages of Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Be%C4%8Dko_izdanje_Gorskog_vijenca_1847.png/250px-Be%C4%8Dko_izdanje_Gorskog_vijenca_1847.png)](./File:Bečko_izdanje_Gorskog_vijenca_1847.png)\\n\\n[The Mountain Wreath](./The_Mountain_Wreath \"The Mountain Wreath\") is a poetic chronicle documenting the struggle of the Montenegrin people for independence from the Ottoman Empire, and is the most famous literary work in the country.\\n\\nThe official language in Montenegro is [Montenegrin](./Montenegrin_language \"Montenegrin language\"). [Serbian](./Serbian_language \"Serbian language\"), [Bosnian](./Bosnian_language \"Bosnian language\"), [Albanian](./Albanian_language \"Albanian language\"), and [Croatian](./Croatian_language \"Croatian language\") are recognised in official usage. Montenegrin, Serbian, Bosnian, and Croatian are [mutually intelligible](./Mutually_intelligible \"Mutually intelligible\") as [standard varieties](./Standard_varieties \"Standard varieties\") of the [Serbo-Croatian language](./Serbo-Croatian_language \"Serbo-Croatian language\"). Serbian is the most spoken language in the country, as a plurality of the population at 43.18% consider it as their [native language](./Native_language \"Native language\"), while 34.52% speaks the Montenegrin language. There is also significant number of people speaking Bosnian (6.98%), Albanian (5.25%), and [Russian](./Russian_language \"Russian language\") (2.36%).[[169]](./Montenegro#cite_note-q454-175)\\n\\n### Religion\\n\\nMain article: [Religion in Montenegro](./Religion_in_Montenegro \"Religion in Montenegro\")\\n\\n\\n\\nReligion in Montenegro ([ARDA](./Association_of_Religion_Data_Archives \"Association of Religion Data Archives\") 2020 est.)[[170]](./Montenegro#cite_note-176)\\n\\n1. [Orthodox](./Eastern_Orthodox \"Eastern Orthodox\") (70.7%)\\n2. [Catholic](./Catholic \"Catholic\") (2.96%)\\n3. [Protestant](./Protestant \"Protestant\") (2.91%)\\n4. [Other Christian](./Christianity \"Christianity\") (2.15%)\\n5. [Sunni](./Sunni \"Sunni\") (17.9%)\\n6. [None](./Irreligion \"Irreligion\") (3.43%)\\n7. Other (0.01%)\\n\\nMontenegro has historically stood at the crossroads of multiculturalism, and over centuries this has shaped its unique co-existence between its Christian and Muslim populations.[[171]](./Montenegro#cite_note-177) Montenegrins have throughout history been [Eastern Orthodox Christians](./Eastern_Orthodox_Christians \"Eastern Orthodox Christians\") that are members of the [Serbian Orthodox Church](./Serbian_Orthodox_Church \"Serbian Orthodox Church\"), which is governed by the [Metropolitanate of Montenegro and the Littoral](./Metropolitanate_of_Montenegro_and_the_Littoral \"Metropolitanate of Montenegro and the Littoral\") and the [Eparchy of Budimlja and Nikšić](./Eparchy_of_Budimlja_and_Nikšić \"Eparchy of Budimlja and Nikšić\").[[172]](./Montenegro#cite_note-Evropa_2021_i808-178) [Eastern Orthodox Christianity](./Eastern_Orthodoxy_in_Montenegro \"Eastern Orthodoxy in Montenegro\") is the predominant religion in Montenegro, with 71.1% of the population adhering to the religion.[[173]](./Montenegro#cite_note-p282-179) Meanwhile, the Serbian Orthodox Church is the largest and most popular church, with approximately 90% of Orthodox Christians in Montenegro following the church.[[174]](./Montenegro#cite_note-United_States_Department_of_State_2021_x826-180) A [schismatic](./Schism_in_Christianity \"Schism in Christianity\") church called The [Montenegrin Orthodox Church](./Montenegrin_Orthodox_Church \"Montenegrin Orthodox Church\"), which broke off from the Serbian Orthodox church in 1993, is followed by the remaining 10% of Orthodox Christians in the country. It also has not been officially recognised by the [Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople](./Ecumenical_Patriarchate_of_Constantinople \"Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople\") and is not in communion with any other canonical Orthodox Christian Church.[[175]](./Montenegro#cite_note-vijesti.me_2019_u217-181)\\n\\nDespite tensions between religious groups during the [Bosnian War](./Bosnian_War \"Bosnian War\"), Montenegro remained fairly stable, mainly due to its population\\'s perspective on religious tolerance and faith diversity.[[176]](./Montenegro#cite_note-182) Religious institutions have guaranteed rights and are separate from the state. The second largest religion is [Islam](./Islam_in_Montenegro \"Islam in Montenegro\"), practiced by 19% of the population. Montenegro has one of the highest proportion of Muslims in Europe and the third highest proportion among Slavic countries, behind only Bosnia and Herzegovina and North Macedonia. A little more than one-fourth of the country\\'s [Albanians](./Albanians \"Albanians\") are [Catholics](./Catholics \"Catholics\") (8,126 in the 2003 census) while the rest (22,267) are mainly [Sunni Muslims](./Sunni_Muslims \"Sunni Muslims\"); in 2012 a protocol recognised [Islam](./Islam \"Islam\") as an official religion, which ensures that [halal](./Halal \"Halal\") foods are served at military facilities, hospitals, dormitories and social facilities; and that Muslim women are permitted to wear headscarves in schools and at public institutions, as well as ensuring that Muslims have the right to take Fridays off for the [Jumu\\'ah](./Jumu\\'ah \"Jumu\\'ah\") (Friday)-prayer.[[177]](./Montenegro#cite_note-183) Since the time of [Vojislavljević dynasty](./Vojislavljević_dynasty \"Vojislavljević dynasty\") Catholicism is autochthonous in the Montenegrin area.[[178]](./Montenegro#cite_note-184) A small Roman Catholic population, mostly Albanians with some Croats, is divided between the [Archdiocese of Antivari](./Archdiocese_of_Antivari \"Archdiocese of Antivari\") headed by the Primate of Serbia and the [Diocese of Kotor](./Diocese_of_Kotor \"Diocese of Kotor\") that is a part of the [Catholic Church in Croatia](./Catholic_Church_in_Croatia \"Catholic Church in Croatia\").\\n\\nCulture\\n-------\\n\\nMain article: [Culture of Montenegro](./Culture_of_Montenegro \"Culture of Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ef/2023_Cetinje_National_Museum.jpg/250px-2023_Cetinje_National_Museum.jpg)](./File:2023_Cetinje_National_Museum.jpg)\\n\\n[National Museum of Montenegro](./National_Museum_of_Montenegro \"National Museum of Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/24/Tripundan_2023_%2804%29.jpg/250px-Tripundan_2023_%2804%29.jpg)](./File:Tripundan_2023_(04).jpg)\\n\\nBoka Navy, from 2021 part of intangible [World Heritage](./World_Heritage \"World Heritage\") UNESCO\\n\\nMontenegrin culture has been shaped most importantly by Orthodox, Ottoman (Turk), Slavic, Central European, and seafaring Adriatic cultures (notably parts of Italy, like the [Republic of Venice](./Republic_of_Venice \"Republic of Venice\")).\\n\\nMontenegro has many significant cultural and historical sites, including heritage sites from the pre-[Romanesque](./Romanesque_architecture \"Romanesque architecture\"), [Gothic](./Gothic_art \"Gothic art\") and [Baroque](./Baroque \"Baroque\") periods. The Montenegrin coastal region is known for its religious monuments, including the [Cathedral of Saint Tryphon](./Cathedral_of_Saint_Tryphon \"Cathedral of Saint Tryphon\") in [Kotor](./Kotor \"Kotor\")[[179]](./Montenegro#cite_note-185) (Cattaro under the Venetians), the basilica of St. Luke (over 800 years), [Our Lady of the Rocks](./Our_Lady_of_the_Rocks \"Our Lady of the Rocks\") (Škrpjela), the [Savina Monastery](./Savina_monastery_(Montenegro) \"Savina monastery (Montenegro)\") and others. Medieval monasteries contain many artistically important frescoes.\\n\\nOne cultural dimension is the ethical ideal of *Čojstvo i Junaštvo*, \"Humaneness and Gallantry\".[[180]](./Montenegro#cite_note-186)[[181]](./Montenegro#cite_note-187) The traditional folk dance of the Montenegrins is the [Oro](./Oro_(eagle_dance) \"Oro (eagle dance)\"), the \"eagle dance\" that involves dancing in circles with couples alternating in the centre, and is finished by forming a human pyramid of dancers standing on each other\\'s shoulders.\\n\\n### Media\\n\\nMain article: [Media of Montenegro](./Media_of_Montenegro \"Media of Montenegro\")\\n\\nTelevision, magazines, and newspapers are operated by both state-owned and for-profit corporations that depend on advertising, [subscription](./Subscription \"Subscription\"), and other sales-related revenues. The [Constitution of Montenegro](./Constitution_of_Montenegro \"Constitution of Montenegro\") guarantees freedom of speech. Montenegro\\'s media system is under transformation, along with the rest of the country. The privately owned media outlet [Vijesti](./Vijesti \"Vijesti\") (*News*) has been the most watched in Montenegro for many years, followed by the state-owned [Radio and Television of Montenegro](./Radio_and_Television_of_Montenegro \"Radio and Television of Montenegro\") (*Radio-televizija Crne Gore, RTCG*). *RTCG* also provides radio and television broadcasts of daily news in the Albanian language.\\n\\n### Sport\\n\\nMain article: [Sport in Montenegro](./Sport_in_Montenegro \"Sport in Montenegro\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cf/Sports_Center_Moraca.jpg/250px-Sports_Center_Moraca.jpg)](./File:Sports_Center_Moraca.jpg)\\n\\nExterior of the [Morača Sports Center](./Morača_Sports_Center \"Morača Sports Center\")\\n\\nSport in Montenegro revolves mostly around [team sports](./Team_sport \"Team sport\"), such as [water polo](./Water_polo \"Water polo\"), [football](./Association_football \"Association football\"), [basketball](./Basketball \"Basketball\"), [handball](./Handball \"Handball\"), and [volleyball](./Volleyball \"Volleyball\"). Other sports involved are [boxing](./Boxing \"Boxing\"), [tennis](./Tennis \"Tennis\"), swimming, [judo](./Judo \"Judo\"), [karate](./Karate \"Karate\"), [athletics](./Athletics_(sport) \"Athletics (sport)\"), [table tennis](./Table_tennis \"Table tennis\"), and [chess](./Chess \"Chess\").\\n\\n[Water polo](./Water_polo \"Water polo\") is the most popular and is considered the [national sport](./National_sport \"National sport\").[[182]](./Montenegro#cite_note-Popular_Sports-188) [Montenegro men\\'s national water polo team](./Montenegro_men\\'s_national_water_polo_team \"Montenegro men\\'s national water polo team\") is one of the world\\'s [top ranked](./FINA_Water_Polo_World_Rankings \"FINA Water Polo World Rankings\") teams, winning the gold medal at the [2008 Men\\'s European Water Polo Championship](./2008_Men\\'s_European_Water_Polo_Championship \"2008 Men\\'s European Water Polo Championship\") in [Málaga](./Málaga \"Málaga\"), Spain, and winning the gold medal at the [2009 FINA Men\\'s Water Polo World League](./2009_FINA_Men\\'s_Water_Polo_World_League \"2009 FINA Men\\'s Water Polo World League\"), held in [Podgorica](./Podgorica \"Podgorica\"). The Montenegrin team [PVK Primorac](./PVK_Primorac \"PVK Primorac\") from [Kotor](./Kotor \"Kotor\") became a champion of Europe at the [LEN Euroleague](./LEN_Euroleague \"LEN Euroleague\") 2009 in [Rijeka](./Rijeka \"Rijeka\"), Croatia. Montenegro came fourth in the men\\'s water polo in the [2016 Olympics](./Water_polo_at_the_2016_Summer_Olympics \"Water polo at the 2016 Summer Olympics\").\\n\\n[Football](./Association_football \"Association football\") is the second most popular sport.[[182]](./Montenegro#cite_note-Popular_Sports-188) The [Montenegro national football team](./Montenegro_national_football_team \"Montenegro national football team\"), founded in 2006, played in playoffs for [UEFA Euro 2012](./UEFA_Euro_2012 \"UEFA Euro 2012\"), its highest play appearance. The [Montenegro national basketball team](./Montenegro_national_basketball_team \"Montenegro national basketball team\") is known for good performances and won many medals as part of the [Yugoslavia national basketball team](./Yugoslavia_national_basketball_team \"Yugoslavia national basketball team\"). In 2006, the [Basketball Federation of Montenegro](./Basketball_Federation_of_Montenegro \"Basketball Federation of Montenegro\") along with this team joined the [International Basketball Federation](./International_Basketball_Federation \"International Basketball Federation\") (FIBA) on its own, following the [Independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 \"Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006\"). Montenegro participated in two [EuroBaskets](./EuroBasket \"EuroBasket\").\\n\\nAmong women sports, [the national handball team](./Montenegro_women\\'s_national_handball_team \"Montenegro women\\'s national handball team\") is the most successful, winning the country\\'s first Olympic medal, claiming silver at the [2012 Summer Olympics](./Handball_at_the_2012_Summer_Olympics \"Handball at the 2012 Summer Olympics\"). This was followed by the [2012 European Championship](./2012_European_Women\\'s_Handball_Championship \"2012 European Women\\'s Handball Championship\") which Montenegro won, becoming European champions. [ŽRK Budućnost Podgorica](./ŽRK_Budućnost_Podgorica \"ŽRK Budućnost Podgorica\") has twice won the EHF Champions League. Montenegro was one of the host countries for the [2022 European Women\\'s Handball Championship](./2022_European_Women\\'s_Handball_Championship \"2022 European Women\\'s Handball Championship\") and came third.\\n\\n### Cuisine\\n\\nMain article: [Montenegrin cuisine](./Montenegrin_cuisine \"Montenegrin cuisine\")\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/13/Foods_from_Montenegro.jpg/250px-Foods_from_Montenegro.jpg)](./File:Foods_from_Montenegro.jpg)\\n\\nFoods from Montenegro\\n\\nThe first major influences to Montenegrin cuisine came from the [Levant](./Levant \"Levant\") and [Turkey](./Turkish_cuisine \"Turkish cuisine\"): [sarma](./Sarma_(food) \"Sarma (food)\"), [musaka](./Musaka \"Musaka\"), [pilav](./Pilav \"Pilav\"), [pita](./Börek#Balkans \"Börek\"), [gibanica](./Gibanica \"Gibanica\"), [burek](./Burek \"Burek\"), [ćevapi](./Ćevapi \"Ćevapi\"), [kebab](./Kebab \"Kebab\"), [đuveč](./Đuveč \"Đuveč\"), and Turkish sweets such as [baklava](./Baklava \"Baklava\") and [tulumba](./Tulumba \"Tulumba\"). [Hungarian cuisine](./Hungarian_cuisine \"Hungarian cuisine\") influences [stews](./Goulash \"Goulash\") and [sataraš](./Sataraš \"Sataraš\"). [Central European cuisine](./Central_European_cuisine \"Central European cuisine\") is evident in the prevalence of [crêpes](./Crêpes \"Crêpes\"), [doughnuts](./Doughnuts \"Doughnuts\"), [jams](./Jam \"Jam\"), many types of [biscuits](./Biscuits \"Biscuits\") and [cakes](./Cakes \"Cakes\"), and various kinds of breads. Montenegrin cuisine also varies geographically; with the cuisine in the coastal area differing from that of the northern highland region. The coastal area is traditionally a representative of [Mediterranean cuisine](./Mediterranean_cuisine \"Mediterranean cuisine\"), with [seafood](./Seafood \"Seafood\") being a common dish. The traditional dishes of Montenegro\\'s [Adriatic coast](./Adriatic_coast \"Adriatic coast\"), unlike its heartland, have been significantly influenced by [Italian](./Italian_cuisine \"Italian cuisine\") cuisine.[[183]](./Montenegro#cite_note-189)\\n\\nSee also\\n--------\\n\\n* ![map](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c6/Europe_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg/40px-Europe_%28orthographic_projection%29.svg.png)[Europe portal](./Portal:Europe \"Portal:Europe\")\\n\\n* [Outline of Montenegro](./Outline_of_Montenegro \"Outline of Montenegro\")\\n* [List of endemic species of Montenegro](./List_of_endemic_species_of_Montenegro \"List of endemic species of Montenegro\")\\n\\nNotes\\n-----\\n\\n1. Extensions | 2012, 2015 |\\n|  | |\\n\\n**Kotor** ([Montenegrin Cyrillic](./Montenegrin_Cyrillic_alphabet \"Montenegrin Cyrillic alphabet\"): Котор, pronounced [[kɔ̌tɔr]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian \"Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian\")), historically known as **Cattaro**[[1]](./Kotor#cite_note-1) (from [Italian](./Italian_language \"Italian language\"), pronounced [[ˈkattaro]](./Help:IPA/Italian \"Help:IPA/Italian\")), is a town in [Coastal region](./Coastal_Montenegro \"Coastal Montenegro\") of [Montenegro](./Montenegro \"Montenegro\"). It is located in a secluded part of the [Bay of Kotor](./Bay_of_Kotor \"Bay of Kotor\"). The city has a population of 13,347 and is the administrative center of [Kotor Municipality](./Kotor_Municipality \"Kotor Municipality\").\\n\\nThe old [Mediterranean](./Mediterranean \"Mediterranean\") port of Kotor is surrounded by [fortifications](./Fortifications_of_Kotor \"Fortifications of Kotor\") built during the [Venetian](./Republic_of_Venice \"Republic of Venice\") period. It is located on the Bay of Kotor (*Boka Kotorska*), one of the most indented parts of the [Adriatic Sea](./Adriatic_Sea \"Adriatic Sea\"), which constitutes a [ria](./Ria \"Ria\"), meaning a submerged river canyon. Together with the nearly overhanging limestone cliffs of [Orjen](./Orjen \"Orjen\") and [Lovćen](./Lovćen \"Lovćen\"), Kotor and its surrounding area form the unique landscape.\\n\\nSince the early 2000s Kotor has seen an increase in tourists,[[2]](./Kotor#cite_note-2) many of them coming by [cruise ship](./Cruise_ship \"Cruise ship\"). Visitors are attracted to the natural environment of the Bay of Kotor and the old town of Kotor. Kotor is part of the [World Heritage Site](./World_Heritage_Site \"World Heritage Site\") dubbed the [Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor](./Natural_and_Culturo-Historical_Region_of_Kotor \"Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor\").\\n\\nThe fortified city of Kotor was also included in [UNESCO](./UNESCO \"UNESCO\")\\'s World Heritage Site list as part of [Venetian Works of Defence between 16th and 17th centuries: *Stato da Terra* – western *Stato da Mar*](./Venetian_Works_of_Defence_between_16th_and_17th_centuries:_Stato_da_Terra_–_western_Stato_da_Mar \"Venetian Works of Defence between 16th and 17th centuries: Stato da Terra – western Stato da Mar\") in 2017.[[3]](./Kotor#cite_note-3)\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n|  |  |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| [icon](./File:Question_book-new.svg) | This section **needs additional citations for [verification](./Wikipedia:Verifiability \"Wikipedia:Verifiability\")**. Montenegro](./Republic_of_Montenegro \"Republic of Montenegro\")) (1992 – 2006)\\n> * ![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/64/Flag_of_Montenegro.svg/40px-Flag_of_Montenegro.svg.png) [Montenegro](./Montenegro \"Montenegro\") (2006 – present)\\n\\n### Early history\\n\\nOnce populated by the [Illyrians](./Illyrians \"Illyrians\"), the exact time of foundation of the first settlement is not known. According to some sources, the oldest settled area dates two millennia back.\\n\\nThe city, first mentioned in 168\\xa0BC, was settled during [ancient Roman](./Ancient_Rome \"Ancient Rome\") times, when it was known as **Acruvium**, **Ascrivium**, or **Ascruvium** ([Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language \"Ancient Greek language\"): Ἀσκρήβιον\\xa0: *Askrḗbion*, [Medieval Greek](./Medieval_Greek_language \"Medieval Greek language\"): Ἀσκρήβιον\\xa0: Askrīvion) and was part of the [Roman province of Dalmatia](./Roman_province_of_Dalmatia \"Roman province of Dalmatia\").[[4]](./Kotor#cite_note-Jackson2010-4)\\n\\n### Middle Ages\\n\\nThe city has been fortified since the early [Middle Ages](./Middle_Ages \"Middle Ages\"), when Emperor [Justinian](./Justinian_I \"Justinian I\") built a fortress above Ascrivium in 535, after expelling the [Ostrogoths](./Ostrogoths \"Ostrogoths\").[[5]](./Kotor#cite_note-5) Ascrivium was plundered by the [Saracens](./Saracens \"Saracens\") in 840. It was further fortified towards the peak of Saint Ivan by [Constantine VII Porphyrogennetos](./Constantine_VII \"Constantine VII\") in the 10th century.\\n\\nIt was one of the more influential [Dalmatian city-states](./Dalmatian_city-states \"Dalmatian city-states\"), initially with a Romance-speaking population, as throughout the early Middle Ages, and until the 11th century the [Dalmatian language](./Dalmatian_language \"Dalmatian language\") was still spoken in Kotor. The city was part of Byzantine Dalmatia in that period, and the modern name of Kotor probably originated in the Byzantine name for the city: *Dekatera* or *Dekaderon*.\\n\\nIn 1002, the city suffered damage under the occupation of the [First Bulgarian Empire](./First_Bulgarian_Empire \"First Bulgarian Empire\"), and in the following year it was ceded to [Duklja](./Duklja \"Duklja\") by the Bulgarian [Tsar Samuil](./Tsar_Samuil \"Tsar Samuil\"). Duklja, or Dioclea, was a vassal duchy of the Bulgarian Empire at the time. The local population resisted the pact and, taking advantage of its alliance with [Dubrovnik](./Republic_of_Ragusa \"Republic of Ragusa\"), maintained its high autonomy. Duklja, the biggest Serb duchy at the time, gradually became more powerful under [Vojislavljević dynasty](./Vojislavljević_dynasty \"Vojislavljević dynasty\") and eventually independent from Byzantium in 1040. The city remained autonomous up until Duklja was once again subdued by Byzantium in 1143.\\n\\nThe city was conquered in 1185 by [Stefan Nemanja](./Stefan_Nemanja \"Stefan Nemanja\"), the ruler of the [Grand Principality of Serbia](./Grand_Principality_of_Serbia \"Grand Principality of Serbia\") and founder of the [Nemanjić dynasty](./Nemanjić_dynasty \"Nemanjić dynasty\"). At that time Kotor was already an episcopal see subordinated to the archbishopric of [Bari](./Bari \"Bari\"), and in the 13th century, [Dominican](./Dominican_Order \"Dominican Order\") and [Franciscan](./Franciscan \"Franciscan\") monasteries were established to check the spread of [Bogomilism](./Bogomilism \"Bogomilism\"). Under the rule of the Nemanjić, Kotor became a partially autonomous city, enjoying many privileges and maintaining its republican institutions. This is evidenced by a statute from 1301, which demonstrates that Kotor had the status of a city under Serbian rule. In the 14th century the commerce of *Cattaro*, as named in Latin scripts (in Serbian *Котор, град краљев/Kotor, grad kraljev/Kotor, city of the King*), rivaled that of Republic of Ragusa, and caused the [Republic of Venice](./Republic_of_Venice \"Republic of Venice\") to be envious. Kotor remained the most important trading port of subsequent Serb states – [Kingdom of Serbia](./Kingdom_of_Serbia_(medieval) \"Kingdom of Serbia (medieval)\") and [Serbian Empire](./Serbian_Empire \"Serbian Empire\"), up to its downfall in 1371.\\n\\nAfter the [fracturing of the Serbian Empire](./Fall_of_the_Serbian_Empire \"Fall of the Serbian Empire\"), the city was taken by the [Kingdom of Hungary](./Kingdom_of_Hungary \"Kingdom of Hungary\"), only to change hands repeatedly between them and the Republic of Venice in the period between 1371 and 1384. After that, Kotor was held by the [Kingdom of Bosnia](./Kingdom_of_Bosnia \"Kingdom of Bosnia\") under [Tvrtko I Kotromanić](./Tvrtko_I_Kotromanić \"Tvrtko I Kotromanić\") between 1384 and 1391. The king of Bosnia, who claimed the Serbian throne, minted his coins in Kotor.\\n\\nAfter the death of Tvrtko in 1391, Kotor became fully independent, until the administration, wary of the looming [Ottoman](./Ottoman_Turks \"Ottoman Turks\") danger, asked Venice for protection. The city acknowledged the [suzerainty](./Suzerainty \"Suzerainty\") of Venice in 1420.\\n\\n### Venetian rule\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Kotor-Montenegro-Scurda.jpg/250px-Kotor-Montenegro-Scurda.jpg)](./File:Kotor-Montenegro-Scurda.jpg)\\n\\nVenetian [Fortifications of Kotor](./Fortifications_of_Kotor \"Fortifications of Kotor\"), UNESCO site\\n\\nThe city was part of the [Venetian Albania](./Venetian_Albania \"Venetian Albania\") province of the [Venetian Republic](./Venetian_Republic \"Venetian Republic\") from 1420 to 1797.\\n\\nFour centuries of Venetian domination have given the city the typical Venetian architecture, that contributes to make Kotor a [UNESCO](./UNESCO \"UNESCO\") world heritage site.[[6]](./Kotor#cite_note-unesco_kotor-6)\\n\\nIn the 14th and 15th centuries, there was an influx of settlers from the oblasts of [Trebinje](./Trebinje \"Trebinje\") (the region around forts Klobuk Ledenica and Rudina) and the *[Duchy of Saint Sava](./Duchy_of_Saint_Sava \"Duchy of Saint Sava\")* ([Gacko](./Gacko \"Gacko\") and [Dabar](./Dabar_(Herzegovina) \"Dabar (Herzegovina)\")) to Kotor.[[7]](./Kotor#cite_note-7) The Italian name of the city is *Cattaro*. Under Venetian rule, Kotor was besieged by the [Ottoman Empire](./Ottoman_Empire \"Ottoman Empire\") in [1538](./Ottoman–Venetian_War_(1537–1540) \"Ottoman–Venetian War (1537–1540)\") and 1657, endured the [plague](./Plague_(disease) \"Plague (disease)\") in 1572, and was nearly destroyed by [earthquakes](./Earthquake \"Earthquake\") in 1563 and [1667](./1667_Dubrovnik_earthquake \"1667 Dubrovnik earthquake\").\\n\\nIn the 15th and 16th centuries, the customs of the local administration of Kotor, such as the right of the *popolari* to elect urban representatives, were unchanged and tolerated by the [Provveditore](./Provveditore \"Provveditore\") of the city, despite Venetian laws prohibiting such institutions. In 1627, during a dispute between the populari and Kotor\\'s nobility, this right was revoked by the *consultare* [Fulgenzio Micanzio](./Fulgenzio_Micanzio \"Fulgenzio Micanzio\"), thus empowering the position of the city\\'s urban elite.[[8]](./Kotor#cite_note-8)\\n\\nAbove the entrance to the old city Kotor, is a stone relief with the [emblem of Yugoslavia](./Emblem_of_Yugoslavia \"Emblem of Yugoslavia\"). Following the [socialist revolution](./World_War_II_in_Yugoslavia \"World War II in Yugoslavia\"), it replaced a stone relief depiciting the Venetian [lion of St. Mark](./Lion_of_Saint_Mark \"Lion of Saint Mark\").\\n\\n### Habsburg and Napoleonic rule\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Rudolf_von_Alt_-_Der_Domplatz_von_Cattaro_-_1841.jpeg/250px-Rudolf_von_Alt_-_Der_Domplatz_von_Cattaro_-_1841.jpeg)](./File:Rudolf_von_Alt_-_Der_Domplatz_von_Cattaro_-_1841.jpeg)\\n\\nThe Cathedral Square in Cattaro depicted by [Rudolf von Alt](./Rudolf_von_Alt \"Rudolf von Alt\"), 1841\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/56/Napoleonov_novac_kovan_u_Kotoru_1813.png)](./File:Napoleonov_novac_kovan_u_Kotoru_1813.png)\\n\\nNapoleonic coins were minted in 1813 in Kotor\\n\\nAfter the [Treaty of Campo Formio](./Treaty_of_Campo_Formio \"Treaty of Campo Formio\") in 1797, it passed to the [Habsburg monarchy](./Habsburg_monarchy \"Habsburg monarchy\"). However, in 1805, it was assigned to the [French Empire](./First_French_Empire \"First French Empire\")\\'s client state, the [Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy](./Kingdom_of_Italy_(Napoleonic) \"Kingdom of Italy (Napoleonic)\"), by the [Treaty of Pressburg](./Treaty_of_Pressburg_(1805) \"Treaty of Pressburg (1805)\"), although in fact held by a Russian squadron under [Dmitry Senyavin](./Dmitry_Senyavin \"Dmitry Senyavin\"). After the Russians retreated, Kotor was united in 1806 with this Kingdom of Italy and then in 1810 with the French Empire\\'s [Illyrian Provinces](./Illyrian_Provinces \"Illyrian Provinces\"). Kotor was [captured by the British in an attack](./Siege_of_Cattaro \"Siege of Cattaro\") on the Bay led by Commodore John Harper in the brig sloop [HMS\\xa0*Saracen*](./HMS_Saracen_(1812) \"HMS Saracen (1812)\") (18 guns). To seal off Kotor, residents along the shore literally pulled the ship in windless conditions with ropes. *Saracen\\'*s crew later hauled naval 18-pounder guns above Fort St. John, the fortress near Kotor, and were reinforced by Captain William Hoste with his ship [HMS\\xa0*Bacchante*](./HMS_Bacchante_(1811)?action=edit&redlink=1 \"HMS Bacchante (1811)\") (38 guns). The French garrison had no alternative but to surrender, which it did on 5 January 1814.\\n\\nIt was restored to the Habsburgs by the [Congress of Vienna](./Congress_of_Vienna \"Congress of Vienna\"). Until 1918, the town, then known as *Cattaro*, was head of the district of the same name, one of the 13 *Bezirkshauptmannschaften* in the [Kingdom of Dalmatia](./Kingdom_of_Dalmatia \"Kingdom of Dalmatia\").[[9]](./Kotor#cite_note-9)\\n\\n### World War I\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Kotor%2C_Rathaus%2C_Gedenktafel_Matrosenaufstand_1918.jpg/250px-Kotor%2C_Rathaus%2C_Gedenktafel_Matrosenaufstand_1918.jpg)](./File:Kotor,_Rathaus,_Gedenktafel_Matrosenaufstand_1918.jpg)\\n\\nMemorial plaque Cattaro mutiny at Kotor city hall\\n\\nDuring [World War I](./World_War_I \"World War I\"), Cattaro was one of three main bases of the [Austro-Hungarian Navy](./Austro-Hungarian_Navy \"Austro-Hungarian Navy\"), the home port of the Austrian Fifth Fleet, consisting of pre-dreadnought battleships and light cruisers, and a base for Austrian and German submarines. The [Cattaro mutiny](./Cattaro_mutiny \"Cattaro mutiny\") of sailors of the Austro-Hungarian Navy occurred in Kotor starting on 1 February 1918. The mutiny remained isolated and had to be abandoned after three days due to the arrival of loyal troops. Four sailors were subsequently executed according to naval law.[[10]](./Kotor#cite_note-10)\\n\\nThe area was the site of some of the fiercest battles between local Montenegrins and [Austria-Hungary](./Austria-Hungary \"Austria-Hungary\"). The city came under the allied [occupation of the eastern Adriatic](./Occupation_of_the_eastern_Adriatic \"Occupation of the eastern Adriatic\") in 1918. After 1918, the city became a part of [Yugoslavia](./Yugoslavia \"Yugoslavia\") and officially became known as *Kotor*.\\n\\n### World War II\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Kotor_entrance.JPG/250px-Kotor_entrance.JPG)](./File:Kotor_entrance.JPG)\\n\\nEntrance of old city Kotor with post-World War II sign \"What belongs to others we don\\'t want, ours we don\\'t give.\"\\n\\nBetween 1941 and 1943 the [Kingdom of Italy](./Kingdom_of_Italy \"Kingdom of Italy\") annexed the area of Kotor which became one of three provinces of the Italian [Governorate of Dalmatia](./Governorate_of_Dalmatia \"Governorate of Dalmatia\") – the [Province of Cattaro](./Province_of_Cattaro \"Province of Cattaro\")[[11]](./Kotor#cite_note-11) had an area (subdivided in 15 \"Comuni\") of 547\\xa0km2 and a population of 39,800 inhabitants. Most of the city\\'s inhabitants were Orthodox (with some Roman Catholics). After the war the remaining [Dalmatian Italians](./Dalmatian_Italians \"Dalmatian Italians\") of Kotor (300 inhabitants) left Yugoslavia towards Italy ([Istrian-Dalmatian exodus](./Istrian-Dalmatian_exodus \"Istrian-Dalmatian exodus\")).[[12]](./Kotor#cite_note-12)\\n\\nMain sights\\n-----------\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c8/St._Tryphon%27s_Cathedral%2C_Kotor%2C_Montenegro.jpg/250px-St._Tryphon%27s_Cathedral%2C_Kotor%2C_Montenegro.jpg)](./File:St._Tryphon\\'s_Cathedral,_Kotor,_Montenegro.jpg)\\n\\n[St Tryphon\\'s Cathedral](./Cathedral_of_Saint_Tryphon \"Cathedral of Saint Tryphon\")\\n\\nKotor has one of the best preserved medieval old towns in the Adriatic and is a double [Unesco World Heritage Site](./Unesco_World_Heritage_Site \"Unesco World Heritage Site\"): it is part of [Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor](./Natural_and_Culturo-Historical_Region_of_Kotor \"Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor\") and [Venetian Works of Defence between the 16th and 17th centuries: Stato da Terra – western Stato da Mar](./Venetian_Works_of_Defence_between_the_16th_and_17th_centuries:_Stato_da_Terra_–_western_Stato_da_Mar \"Venetian Works of Defence between the 16th and 17th centuries: Stato da Terra – western Stato da Mar\").[[6]](./Kotor#cite_note-unesco_kotor-6)\\n\\nIt is home to numerous sights, such as the [Cathedral of Saint Tryphon](./Cathedral_of_Saint_Tryphon \"Cathedral of Saint Tryphon\") in the old town (built in 1166), and the ancient walls which stretch for 4.5\\xa0km (3\\xa0mi) directly above the city. Sveti Đorđe and Gospa od Škrpijela islets off the coast of [Perast](./Perast \"Perast\") are also among the tourism destinations in the vicinity of Kotor.\\n\\nCulture\\n-------\\n\\nKotor hosts several summer events, such as the *Summer Carnival* or *Bokeljska Noć*. Together with [Budva](./Budva \"Budva\"), and the small town of [Tuzi](./Tuzi \"Tuzi\"), near [Podgorica](./Podgorica \"Podgorica\"), the city hosted the [Federation of European Carnival Cities](./Federation_of_European_Carnival_Cities \"Federation of European Carnival Cities\") (FECC) World Carnival City Congress in May 2009.\\n\\nKotor Festival of Theatre for Children is one of the most important festivals of its kind in Southeast Europe.[[13]](./Kotor#cite_note-13) Thirty years of this manifestation have marked performances by artists from over 30 countries, from 5 continents. It was founded in 1993, not far from the place where the first play for children in the Balkans was performed in 1829. The 2017/18 festival was awarded the EFFE Label by the EFA (European Festivals Association).[[14]](./Kotor#cite_note-14) Kotor Festival is highly regarded in the local community and has a large volunteer base.\\n\\nKotor has a large population of cats that have become a symbol of the city.[[15]](./Kotor#cite_note-15) The city has several cat stores and a cat museum, as well as the Cats\\' Square (*Trg od mačaka*).[[16]](./Kotor#cite_note-16) Water and food is left throughout the city for the cats to feed on, and cardboard boxes are often arranged to be a place for the cats to sleep in.[[17]](./Kotor#cite_note-17) Tourists may notice cats in poor health, which may be due to malnutrition, lack of shelter, fighting, or illness (often a common viral respiratory condition for which medicine is unavailable).[[18]](./Kotor#cite_note-18) The charity Kotor Kitties[[19]](./Kotor#cite_note-19) exists to try and help the cats of Kotor through spaying and neutering. Kotor is described evocatively at the beginning of Marguerite Yourcenar\\'s story \\'Marko\\'s Smile.\\'\\n\\nDemographics\\n------------\\n\\nHistorical population\\n\\n| Year | Pop. | ±% |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| 1848 | 3,550 | — |\\n| 1890 | 5,400 | +52.1% |\\n| 1900 | 5,700 | +5.6% |\\n| 1948 | 14,124 | +147.8% |\\n| 1953 | 15,436 | +9.3% |\\n| 1961 | 16,642 | +7.8% |\\n| 1971 | 18,917 | +13.7% |\\n| 1981 | 20,455 | +8.1% |\\n| 1991 | 22,410 | +9.6% |\\n| 2003 | 22,947 | +2.4% |\\n| 2011 | 22,601 | −1.5% |\\n| 2023 | 21,916 | −3.0% |\\n| Source: pop-stat.mashke.org[[20]](./Kotor#cite_note-20) | | |\\n\\nKotor is the administrative centre of Kotor municipality, which includes the towns of [Risan](./Risan \"Risan\") and Perast, as well as many small hamlets around the [Bay of Kotor](./Bay_of_Kotor \"Bay of Kotor\"), and has a population of 21,916.[[21]](./Kotor#cite_note-Monstat-21)\\n\\nThe town of Kotor itself has 1,360 inhabitants, but the administrative limits of the town encompass only the area of the Old Town. The urban area of Kotor also includes [Dobrota](./Dobrota \"Dobrota\") (7,345) and [Škaljari](./Škaljari \"Škaljari\") (3,342), bringing the population of Kotor\\'s urban area close to 13,000 inhabitants. The total number rises to around 15,000 if the neighbouring hamlets of [Muo](./Muo \"Muo\"), [Prčanj](./Prčanj \"Prčanj\") and [Stoliv](./Stoliv?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Stoliv\") are included. The entire population of [Kotor Municipality](./Kotor_Municipality \"Kotor Municipality\") was 21,916, as of the 2023 census.\\n\\nEthnic composition of the municipality in 2011:[[22]](./Kotor#cite_note-Montenegrin_2011_census-22)\\n\\n| Ethnicity | Number | Percentage |\\n| --- | --- | --- |\\n| [Montenegrins](./Montenegrins \"Montenegrins\") | 11,047 | 48.88% |\\n| [Serbs](./Serbs_of_Montenegro \"Serbs of Montenegro\") | 6,910 | 30.57% |\\n| [Croats](./Croats_of_Montenegro \"Croats of Montenegro\") | 1,553 | 6.87% |\\n| Other/undeclared | 3,091 | 13.68% |\\n| **Total** | 22,601 | 100% |\\n\\nThroughout history, there was a significant [Italian-speaking community](./Dalmatian_Italians \"Dalmatian Italians\") in Kotor. Until the 19th century the main language of Kotor was [Italian](./Italian_language \"Italian language\"),[[23]](./Kotor#cite_note-23) which then began to decline in favour of [Serbian](./Serbian_language \"Serbian language\"). According to the Austrian censuses, there were 623 residents of the central settlement that used [Italian](./Italian_language \"Italian language\") as their *habitual language*[[24]](./Kotor#cite_note-Seton-24) (18.7% of the total population) in 1890, and 257 (8.1%) in 1910.[[25]](./Kotor#cite_note-:02-25) The commune as a whole had 646 (11.9%) Italian speakers in 1890, and 274 (4.6%) in 1910.[[25]](./Kotor#cite_note-:02-25) The majority of the Italian population left the city for Italy after the [Treaty of Rapallo (1920)](./Treaty_of_Rapallo_(1920) \"Treaty of Rapallo (1920)\").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed \"Wikipedia:Citation needed\")*] In 2011, only 31 people declared themselves as Italians, corresponding to 0.14% of the total population.[[26]](./Kotor#cite_note-26)\\n\\nIn 1848, the population of the city of Kotor itself was 3,550 people, of whom 2,384 were [Catholics](./Catholic_Church \"Catholic Church\") and 1,157 were [Orthodox Christians](./Serbian_Orthodox_Church \"Serbian Orthodox Church\"). However, the *Circolo* (administrative area) of which Kotor was the capital had a population of 34,326, of whom the majority (24,498) were Orthodox and a minority (9,819) were Catholic.[[27]](./Kotor#cite_note-27) The population of the city proper increased to 5,400 by 1890 and 5,700 by 1900.[[28]](./Kotor#cite_note-28)\\n\\nAccording to documents from 1900, Kotor had 7,617 Catholics, and 7,207 Orthodox Christians. Kotor is still the seat of the [Catholic](./Catholic \"Catholic\") [Bishopric of Kotor](./Roman_Catholic_Diocese_of_Kotor \"Roman Catholic Diocese of Kotor\"), which covers the entire gulf. In 2011, 78% citizens of Kotor were Orthodox Christians, while 12% were listed as Roman Catholic.\\n\\n* [![Serbian Orthodox Church of St. Nicholas](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/35/Serbian_Orthodox_Church_in_Kotor.jpg/120px-Serbian_Orthodox_Church_in_Kotor.jpg)](./File:Serbian_Orthodox_Church_in_Kotor.jpg \"Serbian Orthodox Church of St. Nicholas\")\\n\\n  [Serbian Orthodox Church of St. Nicholas](./Church_of_St._Nicholas,_Kotor \"Church of St. Nicholas, Kotor\")\\n* [![Blessed Ozana Church](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5c/Catedral_de_Kotor%2C_Kotor%2C_Bah%C3%ADa_de_Kotor%2C_Montenegro%2C_2014-04-19%2C_DD_02.JPG/60px-Catedral_de_Kotor%2C_Kotor%2C_Bah%C3%ADa_de_Kotor%2C_Montenegro%2C_2014-04-19%2C_DD_02.JPG)](./File:Catedral_de_Kotor,_Kotor,_Bahía_de_Kotor,_Montenegro,_2014-04-19,_DD_02.JPG \"Blessed Ozana Church\")\\n\\n  Blessed Ozana Church\\n\\nSource: Statistical Office of Montenegro – MONSTAT, Census 2011[[29]](./Kotor#cite_note-29)\\n\\n| Religion (2011 Census) | Number |\\n| --- | --- |\\n| [Eastern Orthodoxy](./Eastern_Orthodox \"Eastern Orthodox\") | 661 |\\n| [Islam](./Islam \"Islam\") | 0 |\\n| [Catholicism](./Roman_Catholicism \"Roman Catholicism\") | 197 |\\n| Other Christians | 6 |\\n| [Atheism](./Atheism \"Atheism\") | 30 |\\n| Undeclared | 51 |\\n| Other | 6 |\\n\\nSports\\n------\\n\\nThe local football team is [FK Bokelj](./FK_Bokelj \"FK Bokelj\"), who have spent several seasons in the country\\'s [top](./Montenegrin_First_League \"Montenegrin First League\") and [second tiers](./Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\"). They play their home games at the [Stadion pod Vrmcem](./Stadion_pod_Vrmcem \"Stadion pod Vrmcem\").\\n\\nKotor is a national powerhouse of [water polo](./Water_polo \"Water polo\"), which is a popular sport in Montenegro. The team of [Primorac Kotor](./Primorac_Kotor \"Primorac Kotor\") won the [LEN Champions League](./LEN_Champions_League \"LEN Champions League\") in 2009. Another club from Kotor, [VA Cattaro](./VA_Cattaro \"VA Cattaro\"), won the 2010 edition of the [LEN Euro Cup](./LEN_Euro_Cup \"LEN Euro Cup\").\\n\\nTransport\\n---------\\n\\nKotor is connected to the [Adriatic Highway](./Adriatic_Highway \"Adriatic Highway\") and the rest of the coast and inland Montenegro by [Vrmac Tunnel](./Vrmac_Tunnel \"Vrmac Tunnel\"). Inland is reachable by detouring from Adriatic highway at Budva or [Sutomore](./Sutomore \"Sutomore\") (through [Sozina tunnel](./Sozina_tunnel \"Sozina tunnel\")). There is also a historic road connecting Kotor with [Cetinje](./Cetinje \"Cetinje\"), which has views of Kotor bay.\\n\\n[Tivat Airport](./Tivat_Airport \"Tivat Airport\") is 5 kilometres (3.1\\xa0mi) away, and there are regular flights to [Belgrade](./Belgrade \"Belgrade\"), [Moscow](./Moscow \"Moscow\"), [Paris](./Paris \"Paris\") and [London](./London \"London\"). Dozens of charter planes land daily on Tivat airport during the summer season.\\n\\n[Podgorica Airport](./Podgorica_Airport \"Podgorica Airport\") is 65 kilometres (40\\xa0mi) away, and it has regular flights to major European destinations throughout the year.\\n\\nTourism\\n-------\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Cruise_Ships_Arrive_at_Kotor_in_June_2024.jpg/250px-Cruise_Ships_Arrive_at_Kotor_in_June_2024.jpg)](./File:Cruise_Ships_Arrive_at_Kotor_in_June_2024.jpg)\\n\\nCruise Ships Arrive at Kotor in June 2024\\n\\nKotor is one of the most popular tourist destinations in Montenegro due to its well-preserved medieval architecture.[[30]](./Kotor#cite_note-30) In 2019, it welcomed over 250,000 tourists.[[31]](./Kotor#cite_note-31)\\n\\nIn June 2021, the first and only public aquarium in Montenegro, [Aquarium Boka](./Aquarium_Boka \"Aquarium Boka\"), was opened in Kotor.[[32]](./Kotor#cite_note-:0-32) It is the organizational unit of the [Institute for Marine Biology](./Institute_for_Marine_Biology_of_the_University_of_Montenegro?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Institute for Marine Biology of the University of Montenegro\") of the [University of Montenegro](./University_of_Montenegro \"University of Montenegro\"), a unique institution in Montenegro that \"Mediterranean climate\") |\\n| Website | [budva.me](https://www.budva.me) |\\n\\n**Budva** ([Cyrillic](./Cyrillic_script \"Cyrillic script\"): Будва, pronounced [[bûːdv̞a]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian \"Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian\") or [[bûdv̞a]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian \"Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian\")) is a town in the [Coastal region](./Coastal_Montenegro \"Coastal Montenegro\") of [Montenegro](./Montenegro \"Montenegro\"). It had 17,479 inhabitants as of 2023,[[2]](./Budva#cite_note-2) and is the centre of [Budva Municipality](./Budva_Municipality \"Budva Municipality\"). The coastal area around Budva, known as the [Budva Riviera](./Budva_Riviera \"Budva Riviera\"), is the center of Montenegrin tourism, renowned for its well-preserved medieval walled city, sandy beaches, and diverse nightlife. Budva is 2,500 years old, which makes it one of the oldest settlements on the Adriatic coast.[[3]](./Budva#cite_note-3)\\n\\nEtymology\\n---------\\n\\nIn [Serbo-Croatian](./Serbo-Croatian \"Serbo-Croatian\"), the town is known as Будва or *Budva*; in [Italian](./Italian_language \"Italian language\") and [Latin](./Latin \"Latin\") as *Budua*; and in (classical/ancient) [Greek](./Greek_language \"Greek language\") as *Bouthoe* (Βουθόη)[[4]](./Budva#cite_note-4) and *Butua* (Βουτούα).[[5]](./Budva#cite_note-5)\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/Illyrian-Greek_helmet_from_Montenegro_-_Budva_-4th_cBC.png/250px-Illyrian-Greek_helmet_from_Montenegro_-_Budva_-4th_cBC.png)](./File:Illyrian-Greek_helmet_from_Montenegro_-_Budva_-4th_cBC.png)\\n\\n[Illyrian helmet](./Illyrian_type_helmet \"Illyrian type helmet\") from Budva (4th century BC)\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Beauvau_1615_budva_city.jpg/250px-Beauvau_1615_budva_city.jpg)](./File:Beauvau_1615_budva_city.jpg)\\n\\nThe Old town in 1615.\\n\\nA legend recounts that [Bouthoe](./Bouthoe \"Bouthoe\") (Βουθόη - *Bouthoē*) was founded by [Cadmus](./Cadmus \"Cadmus\"), the founder of [Thebes, Greece](./Thebes,_Greece \"Thebes, Greece\"). When exiled from Thebes, he found a shelter in this place for himself and his wife, the goddess [Harmonia](./Harmonia_(mythology) \"Harmonia (mythology)\").\\n\\nThe first record of Budva dates back to the 5th century BC. Originally, the site belonged to the state of Illyria. In the 6th century BC, during the [Greek colonization of the Adriatic](./Greek_colonisation#Ionian_Sea,_Adriatic_Sea,_and_Illyria \"Greek colonisation\"), a Greek [emporium](./Emporium_(antiquity) \"Emporium (antiquity)\") was established. In the 2nd century BC, the area of Budva became part of the [Roman Republic](./Roman_Republic \"Roman Republic\") and from 27 BC, of the [Roman Empire](./Roman_Empire \"Roman Empire\").[[6]](./Budva#cite_note-6) Upon the fall of the Empire and its division into east and west, the defensive barrier that separated the two powers happened to run across this area, subsequently making a lasting impact on the history and culture of this town.\\n\\nIn the 6th century, Budva was part of the [Byzantine Empire](./Byzantine_Empire \"Byzantine Empire\"), and in the following two centuries, [Slavs](./Slavs \"Slavs\") and, to a lesser extent, [Avars](./Avars_(Carpathians) \"Avars (Carpathians)\") began to arrive in the area, mixing with the native Roman population. Budva bay was reportedly known as *Avarorum sinus* (Avar bay\\') during the Avar incursions. In 841, Budva was sacked by Muslim [Saracens](./Saracen \"Saracen\"), who devastated the area.\\n\\nIn the early [Middle Ages](./Middle_Ages \"Middle Ages\"), Budva was ruled by a succession of [Doclean](./Duklja \"Duklja\") kings, as well as Serbian and [Zetan](./Zeta_under_the_Balšići \"Zeta under the Balšići\") aristocrats.\\n\\n[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Budua_%281900%29.jpg/250px-Budua_%281900%29.jpg)](./File:Budua_(1900).jpg)\\n\\nThe Venetian walls of Budua (Budva) on a 1900 postcard\\n\\nc.\\u20091200, it became the see of a [Roman Catholic Diocese of Budua](./Roman_Catholic_Diocese_of_Budua \"Roman Catholic Diocese of Budua\"), which lasted until 1828 and was nominally revived as a Latin [titular bishopric](./Titular_bishopric \"Titular bishopric\").\\nIt was controlled by the [Balšić](./Balšić_noble_family \"Balšić noble family\") family for some decades and was shortly controlled by the [Albanian](./Albanians \"Albanians\") [Zaharia](./Zaharia_family \"Zaharia family\") family in the 14th century.[[7]](./Budva#cite_note-7) The [Venetians](./Republic_of_Venice \"Republic of Venice\") ruled the town for nearly 400 years, from 1420 to 1797. Budva, called *Budua* in those centuries, was part of the [Albania Veneta](./Albania_Veneta \"Albania Veneta\") and was fortified by powerful Venetian walls against [Ottoman](./Ottoman_Empire \"Ottoman Empire\") conquests. According to the historian Luigi Paulucci in his book \"Le Bocche di Cattaro nel 1810\" (The Bay of Kotor in 1810), most of the population spoke the [Venetian language](./Venetian_language \"Venetian language\") until the beginning of the 19th century. One of the most renowned theater librettists and composers, [Cristoforo Ivanovich](./Cristoforo_Ivanovich \"Cristoforo Ivanovich\"), was born in Venetian Budua. Nevertheless, Budva was briefly under Ottoman rule between 1572 and 1573 due to the conquest by [Occhiali](./Occhiali \"Occhiali\").[[8]](./Budva#cite_note-8) It was returned to the Venetians under the conditions of the [Treaty of Constantinople (1573)](./Ottoman–Venetian_War_(1570–1573)#Peace_settlement_and_aftermath \"Ottoman–Venetian War (1570–1573)\").[[9]](./Budva#cite_note-9) In 1675, a French Archaeologist, [Jacob Spon](./Jacob_Spon \"Jacob Spon\"), visited Budva and stated that Budva is like a border between Albanians and Venetians.[[10]](./Budva#cite_note-10)\\n\\nWith the fall of the Republic of Venice in 1797, Budva came under the rule of the [Habsburg monarchy](./Habsburg_monarchy \"Habsburg monarchy\"). During the [Napoleonic Wars](./Napoleonic_Wars \"Napoleonic Wars\"), Montenegrin forces allied with [Russia](./Russia \"Russia\") took control over the city in 1806, only to relinquish the city to France in 1807. French rule lasted until 1813, when Budva (along with [Boka Kotorska](./Boka_Kotorska \"Boka Kotorska\")) was ceded to the [Austrian Empire](./Austrian_Empire \"Austrian Empire\"), which remained in control of the city for the next 100 years.[[11]](./Budva#cite_note-11)\\n\\nA union of [Boka Kotorska](./Bay_of_Kotor \"Bay of Kotor\") (and Budva) with Montenegro took place for a brief period (1813–1814), but from 1814 until the end of [World War I](./World_War_I \"World War I\") in 1918, Budva remained under [Austria-Hungary](./Austria-Hungary \"Austria-Hungary\"). The southernmost fortress in the Austro-Hungarian Empire, [Fort Kosmač](./Fort_Kosmač \"Fort Kosmač\"), was constructed nearby to guard the road from Budva to [Cetinje](./Cetinje \"Cetinje\"). After the war, the Serbian army entered Budva after it was abandoned by Austrian forces, and it came under the [Kingdom of Yugoslavia](./Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia \"Kingdom of Yugoslavia\").[[12]](./Budva#cite_note-12)\\n\\nIn 1941, with the beginning of [World War II](./World_War_II \"World War II\"), Budva was annexed by the [Kingdom of Italy](./Kingdom_of_Italy \"Kingdom of Italy\"). Budva was finally liberated from [Axis rule](./Axis_powers \"Axis powers\") on 22 November 1944 and incorporated into the [Socialist Republic of Montenegro](./Socialist_Republic_of_Montenegro \"Socialist Republic of Montenegro\") (which was a part of the [Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia](./Socialist_Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia \"Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia\")).[[13]](./Budva#cite_note-13)\\n\\nA [catastrophic earthquake struck Budva](./1979_Montenegro_earthquake \"1979 Montenegro earthquake\") on 15 April 1979. Much of the old town was devastated, but today there is little evidence of the catastrophe – almost all the buildings were restored to their original form.\\n\\nMontenegro became an independent country in 2006, with Budva as its primary tourist destination.\\n\\nIn 2022, the city became the center of Ukrainian, Russian, and Turkish immigrants in [Montenegro](./Montenegro \"Montenegro\") after the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](./Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine \"Russian invasion of Ukraine\"), resulting in a sharp population increase.\\n\\n### City Assembly (2024–2028)\\n\\n| Party/Coalition | | Seats | Local government |\\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\\n|  | BND | 9 / 33 | Government |\\n|  | [DPS](./Democratic_Party_of_Socialists_of_Montenegro \"Democratic Party of Socialists of Montenegro\") | 7 / 33 | Support |\\n|  | [ZBCG (NSD–DNP)](./For_the_Future_of_Montenegro \"For the Future of Montenegro\") | 6 / 33 | Opposition |\\n|  | [DCG](./Democratic_Montenegro \"Democratic Montenegro\") | 2 / 33 | Opposition |\\n|  | [SDP](./Social_Democratic_Party_of_Montenegro \"Social Democratic Party of Montenegro\") | 2 / 33 | Government |\\n|  | [PzG](./Đorđe_Zenović?action=edit&redlink=1 \"Đorđe Zenović\") | 2 / 33 | Opposition |\\n|  | [SNP](./Socialist_People\\'s_Party_of_Montenegro \"Socialist People\\'s Party of Montenegro\") | 2 / 33 | Opposition |\\n|  | [PES](./Europe_Now \"Europe Now\") | 1 / 33 | Opposition |\\n|  | [URA](./United_Reform_Action \"United Reform Action\") | 1 / 33 | Government |\\n|  | [NB](./New_Budva?action=edit&redlink=1 \"New Budva\") | 1 / 33 | Opposition |\\n\\n### Mayor\\n\\nThe Mayor of Budva is the head of the town and Municipality of Budva.
