The pressures of the real estate market and neglect of urban planning have resulted in a chronic and severe lack of parking spaces and frequent traffic jams during the summer. Even the water and electricity supply have failed to keep up with the explosive growth in the 2000s, but those issues have since been addressed.

A testament to the urban sprawl, the [city bypass](./Bypass_(road) "Bypass (road)") (Obilaznica, a crescent road that circles the northern ends of Budva field, with ends connecting to the Adriatic Highway) is a bypass only in name, as it is now a busy urban street, swallowed by the city's expanding urban area.

The term *Budvanizacija* ("Budvanization") has been used regionally to denote a form of chaotic and massive urban growth, tailored to the needs of individual land owners and developers, without regard for sustainability or environment.

Tourism
-------

See also: [Budva Riviera (region)](./Budva_Riviera_(region) "Budva Riviera (region)")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/Sveti_Stefan%2C_Montenegro.jpg/250px-Sveti_Stefan%2C_Montenegro.jpg)](./File:Sveti_Stefan,_Montenegro.jpg)

[Sveti Stefan](./Sveti_Stefan "Sveti Stefan"), near Budva

Tourism is the main driver of the economy of Budva. It is a significant tourist destination on the eastern Adriatic, and by far the most popular destination in Montenegro. During 2013, Budva recorded 668,931 tourist visits, and 4,468,913 overnight stays, thus accounting for 44,8% of tourist visits to Montenegro, and 47,5% of its overnight stays.[[17]](./Budva#cite_note-Tourism_statistics_2013-17)

Although Budva is notable for its long history and its well-preserved Old Town, it is not primarily known as a destination for sightseeing or cultural tourism. Unlike [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor") or [Dubrovnik](./Dubrovnik "Dubrovnik"), Budva has an image of a crowded beach resort, with a lively and vibrant atmosphere and a very active nightlife.

### Beaches

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Jaz_beach_11.jpg/250px-Jaz_beach_11.jpg)](./File:Jaz_beach_11.jpg)

[Jaz Beach](./Jaz_Beach "Jaz Beach"), near Budva

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Budva-Muntenegru.plaja_Mogren.jpg/250px-Budva-Muntenegru.plaja_Mogren.jpg)](./File:Budva-Muntenegru.plaja_Mogren.jpg)

Mogren Beach

[Mogren Beach](./Mogren_Beach?action=edit&redlink=1 "Mogren Beach") is arguably the best known and most attractive of the Budva city beaches, nested beneath the cliffs of the Spas hill, between cape Mogren and the [Avala](./Avala_Resort_&_Villas?action=edit&redlink=1 "Avala Resort & Villas") hotel. The beach stretches over 350 metres (1,150 ft) and is divided into two distinct areas, Mogren 1 and Mogren 2. The beach is separated from Budva by the Spas hill and is accessible from the old town by a concrete path running 150 metres (490 ft) along the cliffs. The remains of [Mogren Fortress](./Mogren_Fortress "Mogren Fortress") are accessible from hiking trails from Mogren 2.

Other city beaches include the small [Ričardova Glava Beach](./Ričardova_Glava_Beach?action=edit&redlink=1 "Ričardova Glava Beach") ("Richard's Head") and [Pizana Beach](./Pizana_Beach?action=edit&redlink=1 "Pizana Beach"), next to the Old Town, as well as the 1.6 km (1.0 mi) long Slovenska plaža ([Slav](./Slavs "Slavs") beach), that makes up most of the city's coast.

However, majority of the beaches of Budva Riviera are outside the city itself. [Jaz Beach](./Jaz_Beach "Jaz Beach") is a long and spacious beach west of Budva, its hinterland serving as a popular concert and festival venue, as well as a campground. [Bečići](./Bečići "Bečići") resort town, with its long sandy beach, is situated south-east of the city, separated from Budva by the Zavala peninsula.

Further to the south, numerous small beaches and towns, make up the more high end and exclusive part of Budva Riviera. This is especially true for the famous [Sveti Stefan](./Sveti_Stefan "Sveti Stefan") town, but also for other smaller [Paštrovići](./Paštrovići "Paštrovići") settlements in the area, that once were unassuming fishing villages. The area of Sveti Stefan and Pržno, including Miločer resort with its park and secluded beaches, is considered the most exclusive area of the Montenegrin coast.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

The town of [Petrovac](./Petrovac,_Budva "Petrovac, Budva") and the undeveloped [Buljarica](./Buljarica "Buljarica") field occupy the very south of the Budva municipality.

[Sveti Nikola Island](./Sveti_Nikola_Island "Sveti Nikola Island") is located opposite of Old Town, 1 kilometre (0.6 miles) across the Budva bay. Connected to the mainland via [water bus](./Water_taxi "Water taxi"), the island and its beaches are an excursion site for tourists visiting Budva.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

### Nightlife

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Budva_-_panoramio_%289%29.jpg/250px-Budva_-_panoramio_%289%29.jpg)](./File:Budva_-_panoramio_(9).jpg)

Budva by night

Budva is well known regionally as the capital of nightlife of the eastern Adriatic.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] The first discothèques in Budva started to emerge during the 1980s, as hotel-attached dance clubs. However, the clubbing scene mushroomed in the 1990s, with numerous open-air clubs opening along the Budva sea promenade. This trend continued into the 2000s, with Old Town and its promenade hosting a large number of bars, pubs and restaurants, and two big clubs, [Top Hill](./Top_Hill "Top Hill") and Trocadero, dominating the clubbing scene.

### Other

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Budva_%2826939787035%29.jpg/250px-Budva_%2826939787035%29.jpg)](./File:Budva_(26939787035).jpg)

Panoramic view of Budva's coastline

Budva is home to the Adriatic Fair (Jadranski sajam), the only specialized exhibition venue in Montenegro. It hosts numerous [trade fairs](./Trade_fair "Trade fair") throughout the year, including the only [auto show](./Auto_show "Auto show") in Montenegro, held annually in autumn.

[Gambling](./Gambling "Gambling") tourism is also popular in Budva, as many hotels have attached [casinos](./Casino "Casino"). Maestral hotel and casino in Pržno are particularly popular among international gamblers, but other large hotels have also attracted players from European countries.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] The 2006 [James Bond](./James_Bond "James Bond") film *[Casino Royale](./Casino_Royale_(2006_film) "Casino Royale (2006 film)")* is partly set in the eponymous casino in the fictional Montenegrin Hotel Splendide, thus giving a boost to Budva's profile as a gambling destination.

Budva's [marina](./Marina "Marina"), nestled to the north of the Old Town city walls, contributes to the image of Budva as a [nautical tourism](./Nautical_tourism "Nautical tourism") destination. Luxury [yachts](./Yacht "Yacht") dominate marina berths during the summer, overshadowing small fishing vessels owned by the locals. Budva marina was host to periodic [boat shows](./Boat_show "Boat show"), but in recent years it has been losing primacy to the larger and more luxurious Porto Montenegro.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Budva was the host of the [Class 1 World Powerboat Championship](./Class_1_World_Powerboat_Championship "Class 1 World Powerboat Championship") Grand prix in May 2008.

Culture
-------

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Budva_dancer.JPG/250px-Budva_dancer.JPG)](./File:Budva_dancer.JPG)

Budva dancer

Among the cultural events and establishments in the city, the annual cultural event *Theatre City* (Budva Grad Teatar) is of particular importance. Founded in 1987, and held in July and August every year, this festival transforms the entire Old Town into an open-air venue for a programme of theatre, musical, literary and visual art events and performances.

Another event in Budva was the [Pjesma Mediterana](./Pjesma_Mediterana "Pjesma Mediterana") ("Song of the [Mediterranean](./Mediterranean "Mediterranean")"), annual pop musical festival, held in Budva from 1992 to 2010. Its format was similar to that of [Sanremo Music Festival](./Sanremo_Music_Festival "Sanremo Music Festival"), featuring a competition of previously unreleased songs. The song contest attracted performers from the [EX Yugoslavia](./SFRY "SFRY") region. However, the festival was cancelled in 2011 due to lack of funds, and has not been renewed since.

In 2014, the [Sea Dance Festival](./Sea_Dance_Festival "Sea Dance Festival") was organized at Budva's [Jaz Beach](./Jaz_Beach "Jaz Beach") for the first time.[[19]](./Budva#cite_note-19) A spin-off of the [Exit](./Exit_(festival) "Exit (festival)") festival, Sea Dance is set to be an annual event. Jaz Beach rose to prominence as a concert and festival venue with [The Rolling Stones](./The_Rolling_Stones "The Rolling Stones") concert held on 9 July 2007. The show was part of their [A Bigger Bang Tour](./A_Bigger_Bang_Tour#Tour_dates "A Bigger Bang Tour") and attracted a crowd of some 35,000 spectators, twice the population of Budva town itself. [Madonna](./Madonna_(entertainer) "Madonna (entertainer)") staged a show attended by 47,000 spectators at the same venue on 25 September 2008, while [Lenny Kravitz](./Lenny_Kravitz "Lenny Kravitz") and [Armand Van Helden](./Armand_Van_Helden "Armand Van Helden") performed at Jaz beach during the "Live Fest" in August 2008, along with [Goran Bregović](./Goran_Bregović "Goran Bregović"), [Dino Merlin](./Dino_Merlin "Dino Merlin") and [Zdravko Čolić](./Zdravko_Čolić "Zdravko Čolić").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Budva [Carnival](./Carnival "Carnival") is a three-day long festive event in Budva, happening annually during late April or early May. It has been organized every year since 2003, and although a recent carnival, it has attracted significant regional attention. Budva, together with nearby [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"), was host to the [Federation of European Carnival Cities](./Federation_of_European_Carnival_Cities "Federation of European Carnival Cities") (FECC) World Carnival City Congress in May 2009.

Budva city museum is one of the prominent cultural institutions in the city, featuring permanent archaeological and ethnographic exhibits. [Stefan Mitrov Ljubiša](./Stjepan_Mitrov_Ljubiša "Stjepan Mitrov Ljubiša") memorial home is another significant institution, honoring the legacy of the famous native of Budva.

Budva occupies a significant place in the history of the [cinema of Montenegro](./Cinema_of_Montenegro "Cinema of Montenegro"), as it was home to the Zeta Film, the Montenegrin primary motion picture company from the Yugoslav era. The now-defunct company has produced numerous Yugoslav movies, including pictures by the Montenegrin director [Živko Nikolić](./Živko_Nikolić "Živko Nikolić"). Zeta Film was privatized in 2004, and its building was converted to a nightclub, leaving Budva without a single movie theater for a decade. On 30 May 2015, a brand new four screen [multiplex cinema](./Multiplex_(movie_theater) "Multiplex (movie theater)") opened in TQ Plaza shopping mall.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

The city has occasionally provided the backdrop for international movie productions. The 1964 movie *[The Long Ships](./The_Long_Ships_(film) "The Long Ships (film)")* was shot in and around Budva, and the prop from the movie, a large 4m tall cracked [bell](./Bell_(instrument) "Bell (instrument)"), has been permanently displayed in front of the Old Town walls, becoming one of the local landmarks. Recently, Budva has been the setting and the filming location of the locally produced, and regionally popular TV series *Budva na pjenu od mora* (*Budva, on the [sea foam](./Sea_foam "Sea foam")*).[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

### Education

Budva has two elementary schools and one high school. In 2009, city administration founded Knowledge Academy (Akademija Znanja), an institution envisioned to act as a university center and introduce [higher education](./Higher_education "Higher education") to Budva. The Knowledge Academy building, situated in the Rozino neighbourhood of Budva, is currently home to Budva city library and private Business and Tourism faculty, and serves as the center of higher education of the municipality.

### Sports

[FK Mogren](./FK_Mogren "FK Mogren") was the most popular football club in Budva, and the sports club with longest tradition in the city. Founded in 1920, it competed in the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"), winning the championship in 2008–09 and 2010–11. The club also won the Montenegrin Cup of 2008. The club went bankrupt and was expelled in 2017. [Stadion Lugovi](./Stadion_Lugovi "Stadion Lugovi"), the home ground of FK Mogren, will probably be relocated in the near future, as it is situated on a very valuable land lot, right next to the Slovenska beach.

[OFK Petrovac](./OFK_Petrovac "OFK Petrovac"), from the [eponymous town](./Petrovac,_Budva "Petrovac, Budva"), is another significant football team from the Budva municipality.

Another popular sport in Budva is [volleyball](./Volleyball "Volleyball"), with [Budvanska Rivijera](./Budvanska_Rivijera_Budva "Budvanska Rivijera Budva") volleyball team being successful in domestic and international competition. Mediteranski sportski centar ("Mediterranean sports center") is the main indoor sport venue of Budva, and is the home of Budvanska Riviera volleyball team and [RK Budvanska Rivijera](./RK_Budvanska_Rivijera "RK Budvanska Rivijera") [handball](./Handball "Handball") team. The town's basketball team is [KK Mogren](./KK_Mogren "KK Mogren") and [RK Budvanska Rivijera](./RK_Budvanska_Rivijera "RK Budvanska Rivijera") is the handball club.

[Water polo](./Water_polo "Water polo") is a common sport in Budva, as on the rest of the Montenegrin coast. [VK Budva](./VK_Budva "VK Budva") is the city's water polo team, competing in the regional [Adriatic Water Polo League](./Adriatic_Water_Polo_League "Adriatic Water Polo League").

[Paragliding](./Paragliding "Paragliding") is a summer activity in Budva. Steep 700m high hills provide perfect setting and stunning vistas for paragliders, with the hamlet of [Brajići](./Brajići,_Budva "Brajići, Budva") being the usual launching point.[[20]](./Budva#cite_note-20)

Transport
---------

Budva is connected to inland Montenegro by two-laned highways. There are two ways to reach Budva from [Podgorica](./Podgorica "Podgorica") – either through [Cetinje](./Cetinje "Cetinje"), or through the [Sozina tunnel](./Sozina_tunnel "Sozina tunnel") (opened 2005). Either way, Podgorica, the capital and main road junction in Montenegro, is around 60 km (37 mi) away.

Budva is connected to the rest of the coastal towns of Montenegro by the [Adriatic Highway](./Adriatic_Highway "Adriatic Highway"), which extends from [Ulcinj](./Ulcinj "Ulcinj") in the far south to [Herceg Novi](./Herceg_Novi "Herceg Novi") in the north, and on to [Croatia](./Croatia "Croatia").

[Tivat Airport](./Tivat_Airport "Tivat Airport") is 20 km (12 mi) away. There are regular flights to [Belgrade](./Belgrade "Belgrade") and [Moscow](./Moscow "Moscow") throughout the year, and dozens of seasonal and charter flights land daily at the airport during the summer season. [Podgorica Airport](./Podgorica_Airport "Podgorica Airport") is 65 km (40 mi) away, and it has regular flights to a number of European destinations throughout the year.

Urban transport consists of Mediteran Express buses, which operate between Budva's city center and [Sveti Stefan](./Sveti_Stefan "Sveti Stefan"). This line services a large portion of the Budva urban core, as well as some small towns between Budva and Sveti Stefan.

The closest train station is [Sutomore](./Sutomore "Sutomore"). This stop on the [Belgrade–Bar railway](./Belgrade–Bar_railway "Belgrade–Bar railway") is some 30 km (19 mi) away from Budva's city center.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](./Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](./Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](./Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](./Radanovići,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](./Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946–2006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](./FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](./1999–2000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](./OFK_Grbalj#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](./FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](./FK_Budućnost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](./FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](./FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](./Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](./2016–17_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](./FK_Sutjeska_Nikšić "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](./2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](./Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](./Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

**Budva** ([Cyrillic](./Cyrillic_script "Cyrillic script"): Будва, pronounced [[bûːdv̞a]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian") or [[bûdv̞a]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a town in the [Coastal region](./Coastal_Montenegro "Coastal Montenegro") of [Montenegro](./Montenegro "Montenegro"). It had 17,479 inhabitants as of 2023,[[2]](./Budva#cite_note-2) and is the centre of [Budva Municipality](./Budva_Municipality "Budva Municipality"). The coastal area around Budva, known as the [Budva Riviera](./Budva_Riviera "Budva Riviera"), is the center of Montenegrin tourism, renowned for its well-preserved medieval walled city, sandy beaches, and diverse nightlife. Budva is 2,500 years old, which makes it one of the oldest settlements on the Adriatic coast.[[3]](./Budva#cite_note-3)

Etymology
---------

In [Serbo-Croatian](./Serbo-Croatian "Serbo-Croatian"), the town is known as Будва or *Budva*; in [Italian](./Italian_language "Italian language") and [Latin](./Latin "Latin") as *Budua*; and in (classical/ancient) [Greek](./Greek_language "Greek language") as *Bouthoe* (Βουθόη)[[4]](./Budva#cite_note-4) and *Butua* (Βουτούα).[[5]](./Budva#cite_note-5)

History
-------

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6c/Illyrian-Greek_helmet_from_Montenegro_-_Budva_-4th_cBC.png/250px-Illyrian-Greek_helmet_from_Montenegro_-_Budva_-4th_cBC.png)](./File:Illyrian-Greek_helmet_from_Montenegro_-_Budva_-4th_cBC.png)

[Illyrian helmet](./Illyrian_type_helmet "Illyrian type helmet") from Budva (4th century BC)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d9/Beauvau_1615_budva_city.jpg/250px-Beauvau_1615_budva_city.jpg)](./File:Beauvau_1615_budva_city.jpg)

The Old town in 1615.

A legend recounts that [Bouthoe](./Bouthoe "Bouthoe") (Βουθόη - *Bouthoē*) was founded by [Cadmus](./Cadmus "Cadmus"), the founder of [Thebes, Greece](./Thebes,_Greece "Thebes, Greece"). When exiled from Thebes, he found a shelter in this place for himself and his wife, the goddess [Harmonia](./Harmonia_(mythology) "Harmonia (mythology)").

The first record of Budva dates back to the 5th century BC. Originally, the site belonged to the state of Illyria. In the 6th century BC, during the [Greek colonization of the Adriatic](./Greek_colonisation#Ionian_Sea,_Adriatic_Sea,_and_Illyria "Greek colonisation"), a Greek [emporium](./Emporium_(antiquity) "Emporium (antiquity)") was established. In the 2nd century BC, the area of Budva became part of the [Roman Republic](./Roman_Republic "Roman Republic") and from 27 BC, of the [Roman Empire](./Roman_Empire "Roman Empire").[[6]](./Budva#cite_note-6) Upon the fall of the Empire and its division into east and west, the defensive barrier that separated the two powers happened to run across this area, subsequently making a lasting impact on the history and culture of this town.

In the 6th century, Budva was part of the [Byzantine Empire](./Byzantine_Empire "Byzantine Empire"), and in the following two centuries, [Slavs](./Slavs "Slavs") and, to a lesser extent, [Avars](./Avars_(Carpathians) "Avars (Carpathians)") began to arrive in the area, mixing with the native Roman population. Budva bay was reportedly known as *Avarorum sinus* (Avar bay') during the Avar incursions. In 841, Budva was sacked by Muslim [Saracens](./Saracen "Saracen"), who devastated the area.

In the early [Middle Ages](./Middle_Ages "Middle Ages"), Budva was ruled by a succession of [Doclean](./Duklja "Duklja") kings, as well as Serbian and [Zetan](./Zeta_under_the_Balšići "Zeta under the Balšići") aristocrats.

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3b/Budua_%281900%29.jpg/250px-Budua_%281900%29.jpg)](./File:Budua_(1900).jpg)

The Venetian walls of Budua (Budva) on a 1900 postcard

c. 1200, it became the see of a [Roman Catholic Diocese of Budua](./Roman_Catholic_Diocese_of_Budua "Roman Catholic Diocese of Budua"), which lasted until 1828 and was nominally revived as a Latin [titular bishopric](./Titular_bishopric "Titular bishopric").
It was controlled by the [Balšić](./Balšić_noble_family "Balšić noble family") family for some decades and was shortly controlled by the [Albanian](./Albanians "Albanians") [Zaharia](./Zaharia_family "Zaharia family") family in the 14th century.[[7]](./Budva#cite_note-7) The [Venetians](./Republic_of_Venice "Republic of Venice") ruled the town for nearly 400 years, from 1420 to 1797. Budva, called *Budua* in those centuries, was part of the [Albania Veneta](./Albania_Veneta "Albania Veneta") and was fortified by powerful Venetian walls against [Ottoman](./Ottoman_Empire "Ottoman Empire") conquests. According to the historian Luigi Paulucci in his book "Le Bocche di Cattaro nel 1810" (The Bay of Kotor in 1810), most of the population spoke the [Venetian language](./Venetian_language "Venetian language") until the beginning of the 19th century. One of the most renowned theater librettists and composers, [Cristoforo Ivanovich](./Cristoforo_Ivanovich "Cristoforo Ivanovich"), was born in Venetian Budua. Nevertheless, Budva was briefly under Ottoman rule between 1572 and 1573 due to the conquest by [Occhiali](./Occhiali "Occhiali").[[8]](./Budva#cite_note-8) It was returned to the Venetians under the conditions of the [Treaty of Constantinople (1573)](./Ottoman–Venetian_War_(1570–1573)#Peace_settlement_and_aftermath "Ottoman–Venetian War (1570–1573)").[[9]](./Budva#cite_note-9) In 1675, a French Archaeologist, [Jacob Spon](./Jacob_Spon "Jacob Spon"), visited Budva and stated that Budva is like a border between Albanians and Venetians.[[10]](./Budva#cite_note-10)

With the fall of the Republic of Venice in 1797, Budva came under the rule of the [Habsburg monarchy](./Habsburg_monarchy "Habsburg monarchy"). During the [Napoleonic Wars](./Napoleonic_Wars "Napoleonic Wars"), Montenegrin forces allied with [Russia](./Russia "Russia") took control over the city in 1806, only to relinquish the city to France in 1807. French rule lasted until 1813, when Budva (along with [Boka Kotorska](./Boka_Kotorska "Boka Kotorska")) was ceded to the [Austrian Empire](./Austrian_Empire "Austrian Empire"), which remained in control of the city for the next 100 years.[[11]](./Budva#cite_note-11)

A union of [Boka Kotorska](./Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor") (and Budva) with Montenegro took place for a brief period (1813–1814), but from 1814 until the end of [World War I](./World_War_I "World War I") in 1918, Budva remained under [Austria-Hungary](./Austria-Hungary "Austria-Hungary"). The southernmost fortress in the Austro-Hungarian Empire, [Fort Kosmač](./Fort_Kosmač "Fort Kosmač"), was constructed nearby to guard the road from Budva to [Cetinje](./Cetinje "Cetinje"). After the war, the Serbian army entered Budva after it was abandoned by Austrian forces, and it came under the [Kingdom of Yugoslavia](./Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia "Kingdom of Yugoslavia").[[12]](./Budva#cite_note-12)

In 1941, with the beginning of [World War II](./World_War_II "World War II"), Budva was annexed by the [Kingdom of Italy](./Kingdom_of_Italy "Kingdom of Italy"). Budva was finally liberated from [Axis rule](./Axis_powers "Axis powers") on 22 November 1944 and incorporated into the [Socialist Republic of Montenegro](./Socialist_Republic_of_Montenegro "Socialist Republic of Montenegro") (which was a part of the [Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia](./Socialist_Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia")).[[13]](./Budva#cite_note-13)

A [catastrophic earthquake struck Budva](./1979_Montenegro_earthquake "1979 Montenegro earthquake") on 15 April 1979. Much of the old town was devastated, but today there is little evidence of the catastrophe – almost all the buildings were restored to their original form.

Montenegro became an independent country in 2006, with Budva as its primary tourist destination.

In 2022, the city became the center of Ukrainian, Russian, and Turkish immigrants in [Montenegro](./Montenegro "Montenegro") after the [Russian invasion of Ukraine](./Russian_invasion_of_Ukraine "Russian invasion of Ukraine"), resulting in a sharp population increase.

Demographics
------------

Budva is the administrative centre of Budva municipality, which includes the neighbouring towns of [Bečići](./Bečići "Bečići") and [Petrovac](./Petrovac_(Montenegro) "Petrovac (Montenegro)"), and has a population of 19,218 (2011 census).[[1]](./Budva#cite_note-Montenegrin_2011_census-1) The town itself has 13,338 inhabitants.

The Old Town of Budva is situated on a rocky peninsula, on the southern end of Budva field. Archaeological evidence suggests that an [Illyrian](./Illyria "Illyria") settlement was established on the site of the Old Town before [Greek](./Ancient_Greece "Ancient Greece") colonization of the Adriatic. While the site was permanently settled since the Roman era, most of the remaining city walls and buildings were erected during the [Venetian](./Republic_of_Venice "Republic of Venice") rule.

The entire town is encircled with [defensive stone walls](./Defensive_wall "Defensive wall"). The fortifications of Budva are typical of the Medieval walled cities of the Adriatic, complete with [towers](./Fortified_tower "Fortified tower"), [embrasures](./Embrasure "Embrasure"), fortified [city gates](./City_gate "City gate"), and a [citadel](./Citadel "Citadel").

Originally, there were gates on all of the four sides of the walled city. However, sea-facing gates were closed up over the years. The main city gate is Porta di Terra Ferma, the grand entry to the city from the west. It is also the beginning of the city's main thoroughfare, Njegoševa Street. There are also four more gates on the north wall, facing Budva marina (Porta Pizana, Porta Pizana 1 and 2, and Porta Pizanella), and one small gate facing the southwestern beach of Ričardova glava.

The layout of the town is roughly orthogonal, although many streets deviate from the grid, resulting in somewhat irregular pattern, with many [piazzas](./Piazza "Piazza") connected with narrow streets. Today, the entire city within the walls is pedestrian-only.

The town [citadel](./Citadel "Citadel") is situated on the southern tip of the city. Originally known as the Castle of St Mary, the fortification was continually rebuilt and expanded through the Middle Ages, reaching its final form during the Austro-Hungarian rule. The sea-facing 160m long ramparts of the citadel, complete with eastern and western towers, are intricately connected to the rest of the city walls. Austrian stone [barracks](./Barracks "Barracks") form the most prominent structure within the castle, separating the citadel from the rest of the walled city. Ruins of the Santa Maria de Castello church, after which the entire complex was originally named, are located within the citadel.

A large public square is located to the north of the citadel, containing all of the churches of the old town - St. Ivan Church (17th century), Santa Maria in Punta Church (840 AD), St Sava Orthodox Church (12th century), and [The Holy Trinity](./Trinity "Trinity") Orthodox church (1804).

The Old Town suffered extensive damage [in 1979 earthquake](./1979_Montenegro_earthquake "1979 Montenegro earthquake"); repair and reconstruction took eight years (until 1987), but traces of the damage are now hardly noticeable. Today, it is a prime visitor attraction of Budva, packed with tourists during the summer months. Its narrow cobbled streets are lined with restaurants, cafes, pubs and shops.

Although confined to the walls of the Old Town for most of its history, Budva started significant expansion into the adjacent *Budva field* in the 20th century, with the development of the tourism industry. Hotels started springing up near the Old Town and to the west of it, along the 1600m long Slovenska beach, including the landmark Avala hotel (built in 1939), the Mogren hotel, and the Slovenska plaža hotel complex (built in 1984). Development near the Old Town and along the longest city beach was done in a planned and sustainable manner, with parts of Budva built in the [SFRY](./SFRY "SFRY") having all the characteristics of a well-organized resort town. Most of the hotels and facilities built during this period are situated to the south of the town's main traffic artery, a portion of [Adriatic Highway](./Adriatic_Highway "Adriatic Highway") ([E65](./European_route_E65 "European route E65")/[E80](./European_route_E80 "European route E80")) that crosses the city parallel to the Slovenska plaža beach.

However, the rest of the Budva field, to the north of the Adriatic Highway, developed in a less uniform manner. The western part of Budva field, containing a [civic center](./Civic_center "Civic center") (an area featuring local government offices, schools, sports center, police and fire station, health center and bus station), Rozino, Dubovica, and Golubovina neighbourhoods, was developed relatively in accordance with principles of urban planning.

In contrast, the eastern part of the Budva field and the slopes of the hills surrounding it saw the emergence of the chaotic [urban sprawl](./Urban_sprawl "Urban sprawl"). Spontaneous growth began in the late 1980s and early 1990s, as a combination of high demand and inability of the state to enforce urban planning, as the [Breakup of Yugoslavia](./Breakup_of_Yugoslavia "Breakup of Yugoslavia") took place. This trend continued into the 2000s, with prices of real estate skyrocketing following [Montenegrin independence](./Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"). Overwhelming demand, fueled by the influx of foreign capital (in large part from Russia), meant that all the undeveloped lots in the Budva field and surrounding hills were quickly being turned into construction sites. Local and state authorities have failed to keep up with the developers, resulting in the unfortunate lack of urban planning in much of the area. Thus, large parts of Budva are connected with an irregular grid of narrow streets, and have overall inadequate infrastructure. This trend continues even today, with limited land forcing developers to turn to building towering high rises in place of small detached residences that made up for majority of Budva field in the early 1990s.

The pressures of the real estate market and neglect of urban planning have resulted in a chronic and severe lack of parking spaces and frequent traffic jams during the summer. Even the water and electricity supply have failed to keep up with the explosive growth in the 2000s, but those issues have since been addressed.

A testament to the urban sprawl, the [city bypass](./Bypass_(road) "Bypass (road)") (Obilaznica, a crescent road that circles the northern ends of Budva field, with ends connecting to the Adriatic Highway) is a bypass only in name, as it is now a busy urban street, swallowed by the city's expanding urban area.

The term *Budvanizacija* ("Budvanization") has been used regionally to denote a form of chaotic and massive urban growth, tailored to the needs of individual land owners and developers, without regard for sustainability or environment.

Tourism
-------

See also: [Budva Riviera (region)](./Budva_Riviera_(region) "Budva Riviera (region)")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b6/Sveti_Stefan%2C_Montenegro.jpg/250px-Sveti_Stefan%2C_Montenegro.jpg)](./File:Sveti_Stefan,_Montenegro.jpg)

[Sveti Stefan](./Sveti_Stefan "Sveti Stefan"), near Budva

Tourism is the main driver of the economy of Budva. It is a significant tourist destination on the eastern Adriatic, and by far the most popular destination in Montenegro. During 2013, Budva recorded 668,931 tourist visits, and 4,468,913 overnight stays, thus accounting for 44,8% of tourist visits to Montenegro, and 47,5% of its overnight stays.[[17]](./Budva#cite_note-Tourism_statistics_2013-17)

Although Budva is notable for its long history and its well-preserved Old Town, it is not primarily known as a destination for sightseeing or cultural tourism. Unlike [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor") or [Dubrovnik](./Dubrovnik "Dubrovnik"), Budva has an image of a crowded beach resort, with a lively and vibrant atmosphere and a very active nightlife.

### Beaches

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/00/Jaz_beach_11.jpg/250px-Jaz_beach_11.jpg)](./File:Jaz_beach_11.jpg)

[Jaz Beach](./Jaz_Beach "Jaz Beach"), near Budva

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9f/Budva-Muntenegru.plaja_Mogren.jpg/250px-Budva-Muntenegru.plaja_Mogren.jpg)](./File:Budva-Muntenegru.plaja_Mogren.jpg)

Mogren Beach

[Mogren Beach](./Mogren_Beach?action=edit&redlink=1 "Mogren Beach") is arguably the best known and most attractive of the Budva city beaches, nested beneath the cliffs of the Spas hill, between cape Mogren and the [Avala](./Avala_Resort_&_Villas?action=edit&redlink=1 "Avala Resort & Villas") hotel. The beach stretches over 350 metres (1,150 ft) and is divided into two distinct areas, Mogren 1 and Mogren 2. The beach is separated from Budva by the Spas hill and is accessible from the old town by a concrete path running 150 metres (490 ft) along the cliffs. The remains of [Mogren Fortress](./Mogren_Fortress "Mogren Fortress") are accessible from hiking trails from Mogren 2.

Other city beaches include the small [Ričardova Glava Beach](./Ričardova_Glava_Beach?action=edit&redlink=1 "Ričardova Glava Beach") ("Richard's Head") and [Pizana Beach](./Pizana_Beach?action=edit&redlink=1 "Pizana Beach"), next to the Old Town, as well as the 1.6 km (1.0 mi) long Slovenska plaža ([Slav](./Slavs "Slavs") beach), that makes up most of the city's coast.

However, majority of the beaches of Budva Riviera are outside the city itself. [Jaz Beach](./Jaz_Beach "Jaz Beach") is a long and spacious beach west of Budva, its hinterland serving as a popular concert and festival venue, as well as a campground. [Bečići](./Bečići "Bečići") resort town, with its long sandy beach, is situated south-east of the city, separated from Budva by the Zavala peninsula.

Further to the south, numerous small beaches and towns, make up the more high end and exclusive part of Budva Riviera. This is especially true for the famous [Sveti Stefan](./Sveti_Stefan "Sveti Stefan") town, but also for other smaller [Paštrovići](./Paštrovići "Paštrovići") settlements in the area, that once were unassuming fishing villages. The area of Sveti Stefan and Pržno, including Miločer resort with its park and secluded beaches, is considered the most exclusive area of the Montenegrin coast.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

The town of [Petrovac](./Petrovac,_Budva "Petrovac, Budva") and the undeveloped [Buljarica](./Buljarica "Buljarica") field occupy the very south of the Budva municipality.

[Sveti Nikola Island](./Sveti_Nikola_Island "Sveti Nikola Island") is located opposite of Old Town, 1 kilometre (0.6 miles) across the Budva bay. Connected to the mainland via [water bus](./Water_taxi "Water taxi"), the island and its beaches are an excursion site for tourists visiting Budva.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

### Nightlife

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f5/Budva_-_panoramio_%289%29.jpg/250px-Budva_-_panoramio_%289%29.jpg)](./File:Budva_-_panoramio_(9).jpg)

Budva by night

Budva is well known regionally as the capital of nightlife of the eastern Adriatic.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] The first discothèques in Budva started to emerge during the 1980s, as hotel-attached dance clubs. However, the clubbing scene mushroomed in the 1990s, with numerous open-air clubs opening along the Budva sea promenade. This trend continued into the 2000s, with Old Town and its promenade hosting a large number of bars, pubs and restaurants, and two big clubs, [Top Hill](./Top_Hill "Top Hill") and Trocadero, dominating the clubbing scene.

### Other

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Budva_%2826939787035%29.jpg/250px-Budva_%2826939787035%29.jpg)](./File:Budva_(26939787035).jpg)

Panoramic view of Budva's coastline

Budva is home to the Adriatic Fair (Jadranski sajam), the only specialized exhibition venue in Montenegro. It hosts numerous [trade fairs](./Trade_fair "Trade fair") throughout the year, including the only [auto show](./Auto_show "Auto show") in Montenegro, held annually in autumn.

[Gambling](./Gambling "Gambling") tourism is also popular in Budva, as many hotels have attached [casinos](./Casino "Casino"). Maestral hotel and casino in Pržno are particularly popular among international gamblers, but other large hotels have also attracted players from European countries.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] The 2006 [James Bond](./James_Bond "James Bond") film *[Casino Royale](./Casino_Royale_(2006_film) "Casino Royale (2006 film)")* is partly set in the eponymous casino in the fictional Montenegrin Hotel Splendide, thus giving a boost to Budva's profile as a gambling destination.

Budva's [marina](./Marina "Marina"), nestled to the north of the Old Town city walls, contributes to the image of Budva as a [nautical tourism](./Nautical_tourism "Nautical tourism") destination. Luxury [yachts](./Yacht "Yacht") dominate marina berths during the summer, overshadowing small fishing vessels owned by the locals. Budva marina was host to periodic [boat shows](./Boat_show "Boat show"), but in recent years it has been losing primacy to the larger and more luxurious Porto Montenegro.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] Budva was the host of the [Class 1 World Powerboat Championship](./Class_1_World_Powerboat_Championship "Class 1 World Powerboat Championship") Grand prix in May 2008.

Culture
-------

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Budva_dancer.JPG/250px-Budva_dancer.JPG)](./File:Budva_dancer.JPG)

Budva dancer

Among the cultural events and establishments in the city, the annual cultural event *Theatre City* (Budva Grad Teatar) is of particular importance. Founded in 1987, and held in July and August every year, this festival transforms the entire Old Town into an open-air venue for a programme of theatre, musical, literary and visual art events and performances.

Another event in Budva was the [Pjesma Mediterana](./Pjesma_Mediterana "Pjesma Mediterana") ("Song of the [Mediterranean](./Mediterranean "Mediterranean")"), annual pop musical festival, held in Budva from 1992 to 2010. Its format was similar to that of [Sanremo Music Festival](./Sanremo_Music_Festival "Sanremo Music Festival"), featuring a competition of previously unreleased songs. The song contest attracted performers from the [EX Yugoslavia](./SFRY "SFRY") region. However, the festival was cancelled in 2011 due to lack of funds, and has not been renewed since.

In 2014, the [Sea Dance Festival](./Sea_Dance_Festival "Sea Dance Festival") was organized at Budva's [Jaz Beach](./Jaz_Beach "Jaz Beach") for the first time.[[19]](./Budva#cite_note-19) A spin-off of the [Exit](./Exit_(festival) "Exit (festival)") festival, Sea Dance is set to be an annual event. Jaz Beach rose to prominence as a concert and festival venue with [The Rolling Stones](./The_Rolling_Stones "The Rolling Stones") concert held on 9 July 2007. The show was part of their [A Bigger Bang Tour](./A_Bigger_Bang_Tour#Tour_dates "A Bigger Bang Tour") and attracted a crowd of some 35,000 spectators, twice the population of Budva town itself. [Madonna](./Madonna_(entertainer) "Madonna (entertainer)") staged a show attended by 47,000 spectators at the same venue on 25 September 2008, while [Lenny Kravitz](./Lenny_Kravitz "Lenny Kravitz") and [Armand Van Helden](./Armand_Van_Helden "Armand Van Helden") performed at Jaz beach during the "Live Fest" in August 2008, along with [Goran Bregović](./Goran_Bregović "Goran Bregović"), [Dino Merlin](./Dino_Merlin "Dino Merlin") and [Zdravko Čolić](./Zdravko_Čolić "Zdravko Čolić").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

Budva [Carnival](./Carnival "Carnival") is a three-day long festive event in Budva, happening annually during late April or early May. It has been organized every year since 2003, and although a recent carnival, it has attracted significant regional attention. Budva, together with nearby [Kotor](./Kotor "Kotor"), was host to the [Federation of European Carnival Cities](./Federation_of_European_Carnival_Cities "Federation of European Carnival Cities") (FECC) World Carnival City Congress in May 2009.

Budva city museum is one of the prominent cultural institutions in the city, featuring permanent archaeological and ethnographic exhibits. [Stefan Mitrov Ljubiša](./Stjepan_Mitrov_Ljubiša "Stjepan Mitrov Ljubiša") memorial home is another significant institution, honoring the legacy of the famous native of Budva.

Budva occupies a significant place in the history of the [cinema of Montenegro](./Cinema_of_Montenegro "Cinema of Montenegro"), as it was home to the Zeta Film, the Montenegrin primary motion picture company from the Yugoslav era. The now-defunct company has produced numerous Yugoslav movies, including pictures by the Montenegrin director [Živko Nikolić](./Živko_Nikolić "Živko Nikolić"). Zeta Film was privatized in 2004, and its building was converted to a nightclub, leaving Budva without a single movie theater for a decade. On 30 May 2015, a brand new four screen [multiplex cinema](./Multiplex_(movie_theater) "Multiplex (movie theater)") opened in TQ Plaza shopping mall.[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

The city has occasionally provided the backdrop for international movie productions. The 1964 movie *[The Long Ships](./The_Long_Ships_(film) "The Long Ships (film)")* was shot in and around Budva, and the prop from the movie, a large 4m tall cracked [bell](./Bell_(instrument) "Bell (instrument)"), has been permanently displayed in front of the Old Town walls, becoming one of the local landmarks. Recently, Budva has been the setting and the filming location of the locally produced, and regionally popular TV series *Budva na pjenu od mora* (*Budva, on the [sea foam](./Sea_foam "Sea foam")*).[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

### Education

Budva has two elementary schools and one high school. In 2009, city administration founded Knowledge Academy (Akademija Znanja), an institution envisioned to act as a university center and introduce [higher education](./Higher_education "Higher education") to Budva. The Knowledge Academy building, situated in the Rozino neighbourhood of Budva, is currently home to Budva city library and private Business and Tourism faculty, and serves as the center of higher education of the municipality.

### Sports

[FK Mogren](./FK_Mogren "FK Mogren") was the most popular football club in Budva, and the sports club with longest tradition in the city. Founded in 1920, it competed in the [Montenegrin First League](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"), winning the championship in 2008–09 and 2010–11. The club also won the Montenegrin Cup of 2008. The club went bankrupt and was expelled in 2017. [Stadion Lugovi](./Stadion_Lugovi "Stadion Lugovi"), the home ground of FK Mogren, will probably be relocated in the near future, as it is situated on a very valuable land lot, right next to the Slovenska beach.

[OFK Petrovac](./OFK_Petrovac "OFK Petrovac"), from the [eponymous town](./Petrovac,_Budva "Petrovac, Budva"), is another significant football team from the Budva municipality.

Another popular sport in Budva is [volleyball](./Volleyball "Volleyball"), with [Budvanska Rivijera](./Budvanska_Rivijera_Budva "Budvanska Rivijera Budva") volleyball team being successful in domestic and international competition. Mediteranski sportski centar ("Mediterranean sports center") is the main indoor sport venue of Budva, and is the home of Budvanska Riviera volleyball team and [RK Budvanska Rivijera](./RK_Budvanska_Rivijera "RK Budvanska Rivijera") [handball](./Handball "Handball") team. The town's basketball team is [KK Mogren](./KK_Mogren "KK Mogren") and [RK Budvanska Rivijera](./RK_Budvanska_Rivijera "RK Budvanska Rivijera") is the handball club.

[Water polo](./Water_polo "Water polo") is a common sport in Budva, as on the rest of the Montenegrin coast. [VK Budva](./VK_Budva "VK Budva") is the city's water polo team, competing in the regional [Adriatic Water Polo League](./Adriatic_Water_Polo_League "Adriatic Water Polo League").

[Paragliding](./Paragliding "Paragliding") is a summer activity in Budva. Steep 700m high hills provide perfect setting and stunning vistas for paragliders, with the hamlet of [Brajići](./Brajići,_Budva "Brajići, Budva") being the usual launching point.[[20]](./Budva#cite_note-20)

Transport
---------

Budva is connected to inland Montenegro by two-laned highways. There are two ways to reach Budva from [Podgorica](./Podgorica "Podgorica") – either through [Cetinje](./Cetinje "Cetinje"), or through the [Sozina tunnel](./Sozina_tunnel "Sozina tunnel") (opened 2005). Either way, Podgorica, the capital and main road junction in Montenegro, is around 60 km (37 mi) away.

Budva is connected to the rest of the coastal towns of Montenegro by the [Adriatic Highway](./Adriatic_Highway "Adriatic Highway"), which extends from [Ulcinj](./Ulcinj "Ulcinj") in the far south to [Herceg Novi](./Herceg_Novi "Herceg Novi") in the north, and on to [Croatia](./Croatia "Croatia").

[Tivat Airport](./Tivat_Airport "Tivat Airport") is 20 km (12 mi) away. There are regular flights to [Belgrade](./Belgrade "Belgrade") and [Moscow](./Moscow "Moscow") throughout the year, and dozens of seasonal and charter flights land daily at the airport during the summer season. [Podgorica Airport](./Podgorica_Airport "Podgorica Airport") is 65 km (40 mi) away, and it has regular flights to a number of European destinations throughout the year.

Urban transport consists of Mediteran Express buses, which operate between Budva's city center and [Sveti Stefan](./Sveti_Stefan "Sveti Stefan"). This line services a large portion of the Budva urban core, as well as some small towns between Budva and Sveti Stefan.

The closest train station is [Sutomore](./Sutomore "Sutomore"). This stop on the [Belgrade–Bar railway](./Belgrade–Bar_railway "Belgrade–Bar railway") is some 30 km (19 mi) away from Budva's city center.

**Kotor** ([Montenegrin Cyrillic](./Montenegrin_Cyrillic_alphabet "Montenegrin Cyrillic alphabet"): Котор, pronounced [[kɔ̌tɔr]](./Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")), historically known as **Cattaro**[[1]](./Kotor#cite_note-1) (from [Italian](./Italian_language "Italian language"), pronounced [[ˈkattaro]](./Help:IPA/Italian "Help:IPA/Italian")), is a town in [Coastal region](./Coastal_Montenegro "Coastal Montenegro") of [Montenegro](./Montenegro "Montenegro"). It is located in a secluded part of the [Bay of Kotor](./Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor"). The city has a population of 13,347 and is the administrative center of [Kotor Municipality](./Kotor_Municipality "Kotor Municipality").

The old [Mediterranean](./Mediterranean "Mediterranean") port of Kotor is surrounded by [fortifications](./Fortifications_of_Kotor "Fortifications of Kotor") built during the [Venetian](./Republic_of_Venice "Republic of Venice") period. It is located on the Bay of Kotor (*Boka Kotorska*), one of the most indented parts of the [Adriatic Sea](./Adriatic_Sea "Adriatic Sea"), which constitutes a [ria](./Ria "Ria"), meaning a submerged river canyon. Together with the nearly overhanging limestone cliffs of [Orjen](./Orjen "Orjen") and [Lovćen](./Lovćen "Lovćen"), Kotor and its surrounding area form the unique landscape.

Since the early 2000s Kotor has seen an increase in tourists,[[2]](./Kotor#cite_note-2) many of them coming by [cruise ship](./Cruise_ship "Cruise ship"). Visitors are attracted to the natural environment of the Bay of Kotor and the old town of Kotor. Kotor is part of the [World Heritage Site](./World_Heritage_Site "World Heritage Site") dubbed the [Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor](./Natural_and_Culturo-Historical_Region_of_Kotor "Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor").

The fortified city of Kotor was also included in [UNESCO](./UNESCO "UNESCO")'s World Heritage Site list as part of [Venetian Works of Defence between 16th and 17th centuries: *Stato da Terra* – western *Stato da Mar*](./Venetian_Works_of_Defence_between_16th_and_17th_centuries:_Stato_da_Terra_–_western_Stato_da_Mar "Venetian Works of Defence between 16th and 17th centuries: Stato da Terra – western Stato da Mar") in 2017.[[3]](./Kotor#cite_note-3)

### Early history

Once populated by the [Illyrians](./Illyrians "Illyrians"), the exact time of foundation of the first settlement is not known. According to some sources, the oldest settled area dates two millennia back.

The city, first mentioned in 168 BC, was settled during [ancient Roman](./Ancient_Rome "Ancient Rome") times, when it was known as **Acruvium**, **Ascrivium**, or **Ascruvium** ([Ancient Greek](./Ancient_Greek_language "Ancient Greek language"): Ἀσκρήβιον : *Askrḗbion*, [Medieval Greek](./Medieval_Greek_language "Medieval Greek language"): Ἀσκρήβιον : Askrīvion) and was part of the [Roman province of Dalmatia](./Roman_province_of_Dalmatia "Roman province of Dalmatia").[[4]](./Kotor#cite_note-Jackson2010-4)

### Middle Ages

The city has been fortified since the early [Middle Ages](./Middle_Ages "Middle Ages"), when Emperor [Justinian](./Justinian_I "Justinian I") built a fortress above Ascrivium in 535, after expelling the [Ostrogoths](./Ostrogoths "Ostrogoths").[[5]](./Kotor#cite_note-5) Ascrivium was plundered by the [Saracens](./Saracens "Saracens") in 840. It was further fortified towards the peak of Saint Ivan by [Constantine VII Porphyrogennetos](./Constantine_VII "Constantine VII") in the 10th century.

It was one of the more influential [Dalmatian city-states](./Dalmatian_city-states "Dalmatian city-states"), initially with a Romance-speaking population, as throughout the early Middle Ages, and until the 11th century the [Dalmatian language](./Dalmatian_language "Dalmatian language") was still spoken in Kotor. The city was part of Byzantine Dalmatia in that period, and the modern name of Kotor probably originated in the Byzantine name for the city: *Dekatera* or *Dekaderon*.

In 1002, the city suffered damage under the occupation of the [First Bulgarian Empire](./First_Bulgarian_Empire "First Bulgarian Empire"), and in the following year it was ceded to [Duklja](./Duklja "Duklja") by the Bulgarian [Tsar Samuil](./Tsar_Samuil "Tsar Samuil"). Duklja, or Dioclea, was a vassal duchy of the Bulgarian Empire at the time. The local population resisted the pact and, taking advantage of its alliance with [Dubrovnik](./Republic_of_Ragusa "Republic of Ragusa"), maintained its high autonomy. Duklja, the biggest Serb duchy at the time, gradually became more powerful under [Vojislavljević dynasty](./Vojislavljević_dynasty "Vojislavljević dynasty") and eventually independent from Byzantium in 1040. The city remained autonomous up until Duklja was once again subdued by Byzantium in 1143.

The city was conquered in 1185 by [Stefan Nemanja](./Stefan_Nemanja "Stefan Nemanja"), the ruler of the [Grand Principality of Serbia](./Grand_Principality_of_Serbia "Grand Principality of Serbia") and founder of the [Nemanjić dynasty](./Nemanjić_dynasty "Nemanjić dynasty"). At that time Kotor was already an episcopal see subordinated to the archbishopric of [Bari](./Bari "Bari"), and in the 13th century, [Dominican](./Dominican_Order "Dominican Order") and [Franciscan](./Franciscan "Franciscan") monasteries were established to check the spread of [Bogomilism](./Bogomilism "Bogomilism"). Under the rule of the Nemanjić, Kotor became a partially autonomous city, enjoying many privileges and maintaining its republican institutions. This is evidenced by a statute from 1301, which demonstrates that Kotor had the status of a city under Serbian rule. In the 14th century the commerce of *Cattaro*, as named in Latin scripts (in Serbian *Котор, град краљев/Kotor, grad kraljev/Kotor, city of the King*), rivaled that of Republic of Ragusa, and caused the [Republic of Venice](./Republic_of_Venice "Republic of Venice") to be envious. Kotor remained the most important trading port of subsequent Serb states – [Kingdom of Serbia](./Kingdom_of_Serbia_(medieval) "Kingdom of Serbia (medieval)") and [Serbian Empire](./Serbian_Empire "Serbian Empire"), up to its downfall in 1371.

After the [fracturing of the Serbian Empire](./Fall_of_the_Serbian_Empire "Fall of the Serbian Empire"), the city was taken by the [Kingdom of Hungary](./Kingdom_of_Hungary "Kingdom of Hungary"), only to change hands repeatedly between them and the Republic of Venice in the period between 1371 and 1384. After that, Kotor was held by the [Kingdom of Bosnia](./Kingdom_of_Bosnia "Kingdom of Bosnia") under [Tvrtko I Kotromanić](./Tvrtko_I_Kotromanić "Tvrtko I Kotromanić") between 1384 and 1391. The king of Bosnia, who claimed the Serbian throne, minted his coins in Kotor.

After the death of Tvrtko in 1391, Kotor became fully independent, until the administration, wary of the looming [Ottoman](./Ottoman_Turks "Ottoman Turks") danger, asked Venice for protection. The city acknowledged the [suzerainty](./Suzerainty "Suzerainty") of Venice in 1420.

### Venetian rule

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1d/Kotor-Montenegro-Scurda.jpg/250px-Kotor-Montenegro-Scurda.jpg)](./File:Kotor-Montenegro-Scurda.jpg)

Venetian [Fortifications of Kotor](./Fortifications_of_Kotor "Fortifications of Kotor"), UNESCO site

The city was part of the [Venetian Albania](./Venetian_Albania "Venetian Albania") province of the [Venetian Republic](./Venetian_Republic "Venetian Republic") from 1420 to 1797.

Four centuries of Venetian domination have given the city the typical Venetian architecture, that contributes to make Kotor a [UNESCO](./UNESCO "UNESCO") world heritage site.[[6]](./Kotor#cite_note-unesco_kotor-6)

In the 14th and 15th centuries, there was an influx of settlers from the oblasts of [Trebinje](./Trebinje "Trebinje") (the region around forts Klobuk Ledenica and Rudina) and the *[Duchy of Saint Sava](./Duchy_of_Saint_Sava "Duchy of Saint Sava")* ([Gacko](./Gacko "Gacko") and [Dabar](./Dabar_(Herzegovina) "Dabar (Herzegovina)")) to Kotor.[[7]](./Kotor#cite_note-7) The Italian name of the city is *Cattaro*. Under Venetian rule, Kotor was besieged by the [Ottoman Empire](./Ottoman_Empire "Ottoman Empire") in [1538](./Ottoman–Venetian_War_(1537–1540) "Ottoman–Venetian War (1537–1540)") and 1657, endured the [plague](./Plague_(disease) "Plague (disease)") in 1572, and was nearly destroyed by [earthquakes](./Earthquake "Earthquake") in 1563 and [1667](./1667_Dubrovnik_earthquake "1667 Dubrovnik earthquake").

In the 15th and 16th centuries, the customs of the local administration of Kotor, such as the right of the *popolari* to elect urban representatives, were unchanged and tolerated by the [Provveditore](./Provveditore "Provveditore") of the city, despite Venetian laws prohibiting such institutions. In 1627, during a dispute between the populari and Kotor's nobility, this right was revoked by the *consultare* [Fulgenzio Micanzio](./Fulgenzio_Micanzio "Fulgenzio Micanzio"), thus empowering the position of the city's urban elite.[[8]](./Kotor#cite_note-8)

Above the entrance to the old city Kotor, is a stone relief with the [emblem of Yugoslavia](./Emblem_of_Yugoslavia "Emblem of Yugoslavia"). Following the [socialist revolution](./World_War_II_in_Yugoslavia "World War II in Yugoslavia"), it replaced a stone relief depiciting the Venetian [lion of St. Mark](./Lion_of_Saint_Mark "Lion of Saint Mark").

### Habsburg and Napoleonic rule

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Rudolf_von_Alt_-_Der_Domplatz_von_Cattaro_-_1841.jpeg/250px-Rudolf_von_Alt_-_Der_Domplatz_von_Cattaro_-_1841.jpeg)](./File:Rudolf_von_Alt_-_Der_Domplatz_von_Cattaro_-_1841.jpeg)

The Cathedral Square in Cattaro depicted by [Rudolf von Alt](./Rudolf_von_Alt "Rudolf von Alt"), 1841

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/5/56/Napoleonov_novac_kovan_u_Kotoru_1813.png)](./File:Napoleonov_novac_kovan_u_Kotoru_1813.png)

Napoleonic coins were minted in 1813 in Kotor

After the [Treaty of Campo Formio](./Treaty_of_Campo_Formio "Treaty of Campo Formio") in 1797, it passed to the [Habsburg monarchy](./Habsburg_monarchy "Habsburg monarchy"). However, in 1805, it was assigned to the [French Empire](./First_French_Empire "First French Empire")'s client state, the [Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy](./Kingdom_of_Italy_(Napoleonic) "Kingdom of Italy (Napoleonic)"), by the [Treaty of Pressburg](./Treaty_of_Pressburg_(1805) "Treaty of Pressburg (1805)"), although in fact held by a Russian squadron under [Dmitry Senyavin](./Dmitry_Senyavin "Dmitry Senyavin"). After the Russians retreated, Kotor was united in 1806 with this Kingdom of Italy and then in 1810 with the French Empire's [Illyrian Provinces](./Illyrian_Provinces "Illyrian Provinces"). Kotor was [captured by the British in an attack](./Siege_of_Cattaro "Siege of Cattaro") on the Bay led by Commodore John Harper in the brig sloop [HMS *Saracen*](./HMS_Saracen_(1812) "HMS Saracen (1812)") (18 guns). To seal off Kotor, residents along the shore literally pulled the ship in windless conditions with ropes. *Saracen'*s crew later hauled naval 18-pounder guns above Fort St. John, the fortress near Kotor, and were reinforced by Captain William Hoste with his ship [HMS *Bacchante*](./HMS_Bacchante_(1811)?action=edit&redlink=1 "HMS Bacchante (1811)") (38 guns). The French garrison had no alternative but to surrender, which it did on 5 January 1814.

It was restored to the Habsburgs by the [Congress of Vienna](./Congress_of_Vienna "Congress of Vienna"). Until 1918, the town, then known as *Cattaro*, was head of the district of the same name, one of the 13 *Bezirkshauptmannschaften* in the [Kingdom of Dalmatia](./Kingdom_of_Dalmatia "Kingdom of Dalmatia").[[9]](./Kotor#cite_note-9)

### World War I

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ed/Kotor%2C_Rathaus%2C_Gedenktafel_Matrosenaufstand_1918.jpg/250px-Kotor%2C_Rathaus%2C_Gedenktafel_Matrosenaufstand_1918.jpg)](./File:Kotor,_Rathaus,_Gedenktafel_Matrosenaufstand_1918.jpg)

Memorial plaque Cattaro mutiny at Kotor city hall

During [World War I](./World_War_I "World War I"), Cattaro was one of three main bases of the [Austro-Hungarian Navy](./Austro-Hungarian_Navy "Austro-Hungarian Navy"), the home port of the Austrian Fifth Fleet, consisting of pre-dreadnought battleships and light cruisers, and a base for Austrian and German submarines. The [Cattaro mutiny](./Cattaro_mutiny "Cattaro mutiny") of sailors of the Austro-Hungarian Navy occurred in Kotor starting on 1 February 1918. The mutiny remained isolated and had to be abandoned after three days due to the arrival of loyal troops. Four sailors were subsequently executed according to naval law.[[10]](./Kotor#cite_note-10)

The area was the site of some of the fiercest battles between local Montenegrins and [Austria-Hungary](./Austria-Hungary "Austria-Hungary"). The city came under the allied [occupation of the eastern Adriatic](./Occupation_of_the_eastern_Adriatic "Occupation of the eastern Adriatic") in 1918. After 1918, the city became a part of [Yugoslavia](./Yugoslavia "Yugoslavia") and officially became known as *Kotor*.

### World War II

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0f/Kotor_entrance.JPG/250px-Kotor_entrance.JPG)](./File:Kotor_entrance.JPG)

Entrance of old city Kotor with post-World War II sign "What belongs to others we don't want, ours we don't give."

Between 1941 and 1943 the [Kingdom of Italy](./Kingdom_of_Italy "Kingdom of Italy") annexed the area of Kotor which became one of three provinces of the Italian [Governorate of Dalmatia](./Governorate_of_Dalmatia "Governorate of Dalmatia") – the [Province of Cattaro](./Province_of_Cattaro "Province of Cattaro")[[11]](./Kotor#cite_note-11) had an area (subdivided in 15 "Comuni") of 547 km2 and a population of 39,800 inhabitants. Most of the city's inhabitants were Orthodox (with some Roman Catholics). After the war the remaining [Dalmatian Italians](./Dalmatian_Italians "Dalmatian Italians") of Kotor (300 inhabitants) left Yugoslavia towards Italy ([Istrian-Dalmatian exodus](./Istrian-Dalmatian_exodus "Istrian-Dalmatian exodus")).[[12]](./Kotor#cite_note-12)

Main sights
-----------

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c8/St._Tryphon%27s_Cathedral%2C_Kotor%2C_Montenegro.jpg/250px-St._Tryphon%27s_Cathedral%2C_Kotor%2C_Montenegro.jpg)](./File:St._Tryphon's_Cathedral,_Kotor,_Montenegro.jpg)

[St Tryphon's Cathedral](./Cathedral_of_Saint_Tryphon "Cathedral of Saint Tryphon")

Kotor has one of the best preserved medieval old towns in the Adriatic and is a double [Unesco World Heritage Site](./Unesco_World_Heritage_Site "Unesco World Heritage Site"): it is part of [Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor](./Natural_and_Culturo-Historical_Region_of_Kotor "Natural and Culturo-Historical Region of Kotor") and [Venetian Works of Defence between the 16th and 17th centuries: Stato da Terra – western Stato da Mar](./Venetian_Works_of_Defence_between_the_16th_and_17th_centuries:_Stato_da_Terra_–_western_Stato_da_Mar "Venetian Works of Defence between the 16th and 17th centuries: Stato da Terra – western Stato da Mar").[[6]](./Kotor#cite_note-unesco_kotor-6)

It is home to numerous sights, such as the [Cathedral of Saint Tryphon](./Cathedral_of_Saint_Tryphon "Cathedral of Saint Tryphon") in the old town (built in 1166), and the ancient walls which stretch for 4.5 km (3 mi) directly above the city. Sveti Đorđe and Gospa od Škrpijela islets off the coast of [Perast](./Perast "Perast") are also among the tourism destinations in the vicinity of Kotor.

Culture
-------

Kotor hosts several summer events, such as the *Summer Carnival* or *Bokeljska Noć*. Together with [Budva](./Budva "Budva"), and the small town of [Tuzi](./Tuzi "Tuzi"), near [Podgorica](./Podgorica "Podgorica"), the city hosted the [Federation of European Carnival Cities](./Federation_of_European_Carnival_Cities "Federation of European Carnival Cities") (FECC) World Carnival City Congress in May 2009.

Kotor Festival of Theatre for Children is one of the most important festivals of its kind in Southeast Europe.[[13]](./Kotor#cite_note-13) Thirty years of this manifestation have marked performances by artists from over 30 countries, from 5 continents. It was founded in 1993, not far from the place where the first play for children in the Balkans was performed in 1829. The 2017/18 festival was awarded the EFFE Label by the EFA (European Festivals Association).[[14]](./Kotor#cite_note-14) Kotor Festival is highly regarded in the local community and has a large volunteer base.

Kotor has a large population of cats that have become a symbol of the city.[[15]](./Kotor#cite_note-15) The city has several cat stores and a cat museum, as well as the Cats' Square (*Trg od mačaka*).[[16]](./Kotor#cite_note-16) Water and food is left throughout the city for the cats to feed on, and cardboard boxes are often arranged to be a place for the cats to sleep in.[[17]](./Kotor#cite_note-17) Tourists may notice cats in poor health, which may be due to malnutrition, lack of shelter, fighting, or illness (often a common viral respiratory condition for which medicine is unavailable).[[18]](./Kotor#cite_note-18) The charity Kotor Kitties[[19]](./Kotor#cite_note-19) exists to try and help the cats of Kotor through spaying and neutering. Kotor is described evocatively at the beginning of Marguerite Yourcenar's story 'Marko's Smile.'

Kotor is the administrative centre of Kotor municipality, which includes the towns of [Risan](./Risan "Risan") and Perast, as well as many small hamlets around the [Bay of Kotor](./Bay_of_Kotor "Bay of Kotor"), and has a population of 21,916.[[21]](./Kotor#cite_note-Monstat-21)

The town of Kotor itself has 1,360 inhabitants, but the administrative limits of the town encompass only the area of the Old Town. The urban area of Kotor also includes [Dobrota](./Dobrota "Dobrota") (7,345) and [Škaljari](./Škaljari "Škaljari") (3,342), bringing the population of Kotor's urban area close to 13,000 inhabitants. The total number rises to around 15,000 if the neighbouring hamlets of [Muo](./Muo "Muo"), [Prčanj](./Prčanj "Prčanj") and [Stoliv](./Stoliv?action=edit&redlink=1 "Stoliv") are included. The entire population of [Kotor Municipality](./Kotor_Municipality "Kotor Municipality") was 21,916, as of the 2023 census.

Throughout history, there was a significant [Italian-speaking community](./Dalmatian_Italians "Dalmatian Italians") in Kotor. Until the 19th century the main language of Kotor was [Italian](./Italian_language "Italian language"),[[23]](./Kotor#cite_note-23) which then began to decline in favour of [Serbian](./Serbian_language "Serbian language"). According to the Austrian censuses, there were 623 residents of the central settlement that used [Italian](./Italian_language "Italian language") as their *habitual language*[[24]](./Kotor#cite_note-Seton-24) (18.7% of the total population) in 1890, and 257 (8.1%) in 1910.[[25]](./Kotor#cite_note-:02-25) The commune as a whole had 646 (11.9%) Italian speakers in 1890, and 274 (4.6%) in 1910.[[25]](./Kotor#cite_note-:02-25) The majority of the Italian population left the city for Italy after the [Treaty of Rapallo (1920)](./Treaty_of_Rapallo_(1920) "Treaty of Rapallo (1920)").[*[citation needed](./Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] In 2011, only 31 people declared themselves as Italians, corresponding to 0.14% of the total population.[[26]](./Kotor#cite_note-26)

In 1848, the population of the city of Kotor itself was 3,550 people, of whom 2,384 were [Catholics](./Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") and 1,157 were [Orthodox Christians](./Serbian_Orthodox_Church "Serbian Orthodox Church"). However, the *Circolo* (administrative area) of which Kotor was the capital had a population of 34,326, of whom the majority (24,498) were Orthodox and a minority (9,819) were Catholic.[[27]](./Kotor#cite_note-27) The population of the city proper increased to 5,400 by 1890 and 5,700 by 1900.[[28]](./Kotor#cite_note-28)

According to documents from 1900, Kotor had 7,617 Catholics, and 7,207 Orthodox Christians. Kotor is still the seat of the [Catholic](./Catholic "Catholic") [Bishopric of Kotor](./Roman_Catholic_Diocese_of_Kotor "Roman Catholic Diocese of Kotor"), which covers the entire gulf. In 2011, 78% citizens of Kotor were Orthodox Christians, while 12% were listed as Roman Catholic.

Sports
------

The local football team is [FK Bokelj](./FK_Bokelj "FK Bokelj"), who have spent several seasons in the country's [top](./Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League") and [second tiers](./Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League"). They play their home games at the [Stadion pod Vrmcem](./Stadion_pod_Vrmcem "Stadion pod Vrmcem").

Kotor is a national powerhouse of [water polo](./Water_polo "Water polo"), which is a popular sport in Montenegro. The team of [Primorac Kotor](./Primorac_Kotor "Primorac Kotor") won the [LEN Champions League](./LEN_Champions_League "LEN Champions League") in 2009. Another club from Kotor, [VA Cattaro](./VA_Cattaro "VA Cattaro"), won the 2010 edition of the [LEN Euro Cup](./LEN_Euro_Cup "LEN Euro Cup").

Transport
---------

Kotor is connected to the [Adriatic Highway](./Adriatic_Highway "Adriatic Highway") and the rest of the coast and inland Montenegro by [Vrmac Tunnel](./Vrmac_Tunnel "Vrmac Tunnel"). Inland is reachable by detouring from Adriatic highway at Budva or [Sutomore](./Sutomore "Sutomore") (through [Sozina tunnel](./Sozina_tunnel "Sozina tunnel")). There is also a historic road connecting Kotor with [Cetinje](./Cetinje "Cetinje"), which has views of Kotor bay.

[Tivat Airport](./Tivat_Airport "Tivat Airport") is 5 kilometres (3.1 mi) away, and there are regular flights to [Belgrade](./Belgrade "Belgrade"), [Moscow](./Moscow "Moscow"), [Paris](./Paris "Paris") and [London](./London "London"). Dozens of charter planes land daily on Tivat airport during the summer season.

[Podgorica Airport](./Podgorica_Airport "Podgorica Airport") is 65 kilometres (40 mi) away, and it has regular flights to major European destinations throughout the year.

Tourism
-------

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Cruise_Ships_Arrive_at_Kotor_in_June_2024.jpg/250px-Cruise_Ships_Arrive_at_Kotor_in_June_2024.jpg)](./File:Cruise_Ships_Arrive_at_Kotor_in_June_2024.jpg)

Cruise Ships Arrive at Kotor in June 2024

Kotor is one of the most popular tourist destinations in Montenegro due to its well-preserved medieval architecture.[[30]](./Kotor#cite_note-30) In 2019, it welcomed over 250,000 tourists.[[31]](./Kotor#cite_note-31)

In June 2021, the first and only public aquarium in Montenegro, [Aquarium Boka](./Aquarium_Boka "Aquarium Boka"), was opened in Kotor.[[32]](./Kotor#cite_note-:0-32) It is the organizational unit of the [Institute for Marine Biology](./Institute_for_Marine_Biology_of_the_University_of_Montenegro?action=edit&redlink=1 "Institute for Marine Biology of the University of Montenegro") of the [University of Montenegro](./University_of_Montenegro "University of Montenegro"), a unique institution in Montenegro that combines research and education to promote and practice the efficient conservation of marine wildlife.[[33]](./Kotor#cite_note-:1-33) In the first three months, the Aquarium was visited by more than 8,000 people.[[34]](./Kotor#cite_note-34)
